Quote.notes:
Thermal damage and melting at splice locations.
Heat-damaged conductor insulation.
Corroded/oxidized copper conductors.
Damaged rooftop junction box cover.
Potential water intrusion and high-resistance connection failure.
All damaged conductors, connectors, and the junction box should be replaced.



Installation Requirements -

1. Junction Box Mounting
Install new EZ Solar JB-1.2 in the existing rooftop location or approved adjacent location.
Maintain roof flashing and weatherproofing integrity.
Secure box per manufacturer's installation instructions.
Do not mount in a manner that allows standing water accumulation.

2. Conductor Replacement
Remove all conductors exhibiting:
Burned insulation
Carbonization
Corrosion
Thermal damage
Replace damaged conductors back to the nearest point of undamaged insulation.
Use only listed conductors suitable for rooftop PV installations:
THWN-2 Copper in conduit
PV Wire where applicable
Wet-location rated insulation

3. Splicing Requirements
Replace all existing wire connectors within the enclosure.
Use UL-listed connectors rated for:
Stranded copper conductors
Wet locations
Rooftop temperatures
Conductors shall be twisted and terminated per manufacturer instructions.
Verify all splices pass pull-test verification.

4. Grounding and Bonding
Verify continuity of the equipment grounding conductor.
Restore any damaged grounding conductors.
All metal raceways and fittings shall remain bonded.
Quote.scope_of_work:
Scope of Work: Remove and Replace Damaged Rooftop PV Junction Box and Associated Wiring
Remove and dispose of the existing damaged rooftop PV junction box, associated wire connectors, and all heat-damaged conductors within the affected enclosure.

Furnish and install a new EZ Solar JB-1.2 Rooftop PV Junction Box.
Remove and replace the existing Romex cable between the attic and rooftop junction box as required.
Attic Junction Box Installation

Locate the existing splice/junction box within the attic serving the rooftop PV circuit.
If no existing junction box is present and the Romex cable is routed directly through the roof penetration, install a new 4" x 4" steel junction box in an accessible attic location in accordance with NEC requirements.
Extend and splice the replacement Romex conductors within the attic junction box using UL-listed wire connectors to provide sufficient conductor length for proper termination within the new rooftop junction box.
Conductor Inspection and Repair

Inspect all branch-circuit and homerun conductors entering and exiting the rooftop junction box for thermal damage, insulation degradation, corrosion, or other signs of conductor failure.
Replace all damaged conductors back to the nearest point of undamaged insulation and clean copper.
Inspect Enphase AC Q-Cable conductors for heat damage.

If any AC Q-Cable conductors are found to be damaged or too short for proper termination, install manufacturer-approved Enphase male and female field-wireable connectors and splice in new Q-Cable sections as required.
Junction Box Wiring and Terminations
Furnish and install new UL-listed weather-resistant wire connectors, fittings, bushings, cable connectors, and strain-relief components as required.

Re-terminate all conductors using manufacturer-approved methods and torque specifications.
Verify continuity of the equipment grounding conductor and restore all grounding and bonding connections.
Weatherproofing and System Testing

Seal all roof penetrations and junction box entries as required to maintain a weather-tight installation and prevent moisture intrusion.
Perform continuity, polarity, grounding, and voltage verification testing on all repaired circuits.
Re-energize the PV system and verify proper operation of all affected equipment and branch circuits.
Document all findings, repairs performed, and any additional deficiencies discovered during the repair process.

FST: Ethan L. Coleman D.

Customer: Robert Adams
 Site Address: 530 Kitty Fork Road, Clinton, NC 28328, US
 Service Type: Electrical Correction / Gateway Relocation

Findings

• Problem Description: Envoy AB not communicating with microinverters due to long distance between MSP and garage solar equipment. A 120V receptacle was installed at the garage, but no active neutral is present in the garage subpanel. No Wi-Fi is available at the garage for communications.

• Root Cause: Neutral conductor was not run from the MSP to the junction box before the run to the garage.

• Diagnostic Findings: Existing neutral is present from the house junction box to the garage but not from the MSP to the junction box. Communications issues are caused by power and networking limitations at the garage location.


Internal note: 

Root Cause Summary:
 Neutral conductor was not installed between the MSP and house junction box, preventing proper power configuration at the garage location. The remote garage location also lacks Wi-Fi connectivity, resulting in Envoy communication failures.

Key Assumptions:
Existing conduit, junction boxes, and garage electrical equipment remain serviceable.
Cable routing through the crawl space is accessible without major modifications.
Existing neutral conductor from the house junction box to the garage remains intact and usable.
No additional electrical deficiencies or communication equipment failures are present beyond those identified.

Customer Impact:
Restores proper neutral path required for garage electrical configuration.
Re-establishes gateway communications through cellular connectivity where Wi-Fi is unavailable.
Improves system monitoring reliability and remote reporting capabilities..
Quote.scope_of_work:
Install approximately 125 feet of 6/3 Romex cable from the main service panel (MSP) through the crawl space to the existing house junction box to provide the required neutral conductor. Terminate and land conductors, install a Polaris lug to connect to the existing neutral, and restore proper circuit configuration. Install a cellular modem and relocate the gateway to the garage to re-establish reliable system communications where Wi-Fi is unavailable. Complete operational testing to verify proper electrical functionality and monitoring communications

Quote.scope_of_work:
**Scope of Work: Enphase M250 Microinverter Replacement**

**1. Project Objective**
Replace one failed Enphase M250 microinverter identified as non-functional (no AC voltage output) to restore full array performance.

**2. Scope of Tasks**
*   **Site Preparation:** Perform a field safety assessment. Access the array at the identified location per site layout.
*   **Removal:** Disconnect the associated PV module from the failed microinverter. Disconnect the microinverter from the AC trunk cable. Remove the failed unit from the racking system.
*   **Installation:** Mount the replacement Enphase M250 unit to the racking system. Connect the DC leads from the PV module and the AC connector to the trunk cable.
*   **System Integration:** Update the Envoy/Enphase Installer Toolkit to reflect the new serial number (SN) and initiate the replacement process in the Enlighten monitoring platform.
*   **Verification:** Confirm that the Envoy successfully recognizes the new unit. Verify the unit is communicating and reporting AC production.
*   **Post-Installation Check:** Ensure all connections are secure, cable management is restored to original specifications, and the PV module is properly re-secured to the racking.

**3. Safety Considerations**
*   **Electrical Hazard:** Technicians must utilize appropriate PPE, including insulated gloves and voltage-rated tools. All work must follow LOTO (Lockout/Tagout) procedures on the branch circuit breaker prior to handling AC connectors.
*   **Fall Protection:** If performing work on sloped or elevated surfaces, technicians must utilize fall protection equipment (harnesses and lanyards) in accordance with OSHA standards.
*   **DC Safety:** Treat PV modules as live; exercise caution when disconnecting DC leads, as they remain energized in the presence of sunlight.

**4. Methodology**
The technician will utilize a systematic approach: isolate the branch circuit, perform the hardware swap, utilize the Enphase Installer Toolkit for digital commissioning, and conduct a data-validated functional test. Success is defined by the unit reporting normal operational status and production data within the Enphase Enlighten monitoring portal.

### Scope of Work

**Project Title:** Ground Bonding Installation for Rooftop Solar System

**1. Scope of Work Description:**
   - Conduct an inspection of the rooftop solar system to evaluate the existing ground bonding.
   - Complete the installation of the required ground wire to establish a proper ground connection for the solar system.
   - Verify the continuity and integrity of the ground bond following installation using appropriate testing equipment.
   - Document the process, including before and after measurements, to confirm that the installation meets all relevant codes and standards.

**2. Safety Considerations:**
   - Ensure all personnel are equipped with Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), including hard hats, safety glasses, gloves, and slip-resistant footwear.
   - Confirm that the solar system is de-energized before starting work to prevent electrical shock.
   - Use proper fall protection measures when working on the rooftop to minimize the risk of falls.
   - Follow all relevant OSHA regulations and company safety protocols throughout the implementation of the work.

**3. Expected Approach/Methodology:**
   - Access the rooftop solar installation safely via an appropriate ladder or scaffold, ensuring that the pathway is clear of any obstructions.
   - Identify the location for the ground wire connection, and assess existing grounding configurations and materials.
   - Install a properly rated and appropriately sized ground wire, ensuring secure and reliable connections to both the solar array and the building grounding system.
   - Use a multimeter or ground testing equipment to ensure proper continuity of the ground connection.
   - Complete a final inspection and provide documentation of all work performed, including any necessary adjustments or corrections made to existing installations. 

End of Scope of Work.

Quote.scope_of_work:
### Scope of Work: IQ Combiner 5c System Remediation and Electrical Repair

**1. Project Objective**
Removed and install new IQ Combiner 5c. The objective is to restore the system to full operational status by replacing compromised components, rectifying damaged conductors, and ensuring the PVC pathway meets original installation standards. 

**2. Scope of Tasks**
*   **Documentation:** Prior to any disassembly, provide high-resolution photo documentation of all thermal damage to establish a clear record of the incident’s origin. Thermally damaged IQ combiner and all breakers will be removed and mailed back for failure annalysis. 
*   **Component Replacement:** 
    *   Remove and replace the damaged IQ Combiner 5c with new IQ Combiner 5c..
    *   Replace (4) 20A breakers and one (1) 15A breaker affected by the event.
    *   Replace all damaged PVC conduit runs spanning from the System Controller to the IQ Combiner.
*   **Wiring/Conductor Remediation:** 
    *   Replace all compromised wiring associated with the IQ Combiner, including but not limited to: feeder conductors, neutral conductors, communication (bus) wiring, and Current Transformer (CT) leads.
*   **Testing and Commissioning:** 
    *   Perform continuity and insulation resistance testing on all new wire runs.
    *   Verify proper polarity and orientation of CTs.
    *   Recommission the IQ Combiner 5c in the Enphase Installer Toolkit to ensure proper communication with the System Controller and gateway.

**3. Safety Considerations**
*   **LOTO Procedures:** Strict adherence to Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) protocols is mandatory. All power sources, including utility grid and PV array (DC disconnects), must be isolated and verified de-energized before work commences.
*   **PPE Requirements:** Technicians must utilize appropriate Arc Flash PPE (as per NFPA 70E requirements) and insulated hand tools suitable for the voltage levels present.
*   **Site Hazards:** Inspect all surrounding electrical equipment for collateral heat damage or brittle insulation before energization.

**4. Methodology**
*   **System Shutdown:** Execute a full system shutdown and verify zero energy state.
*   **Deconstruction:** Carefully remove thermally compromised conduit and wiring, labeling all circuits to ensure correct termination in the replacement combiner.
*   **Reinstallation:** Install replacement PVC conduits according to NEC requirements, ensuring proper support and weatherproofing. Pull new conductors, maintaining appropriate wire gauge and color coding.
*   **Termination:** Terminate all feeders, neutrals, and communication lines to torque specifications provided by the manufacturer.
*   **Verification:** Perform a final visual inspection of all connections, verify system voltage/phasing, and confirm system reporting via the Enphase monitoring platform.

Quote.scope_of_work:
**Scope of Work: Solar Array Remediation and Critter Damage Repair**

**1. Objective**
Repair damage caused by wildlife nesting beneath the PV array, restore electrical continuity to affected Microinverters (MIs), and install permanent pest-exclusion measures to prevent recurrence.

**2. Scope of Tasks**
*   **Site Decommissioning:** Maintain the string breaker in the "OFF" position and perform Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures at the AC combiner/disconnect to ensure zero-energy state before accessing the roof.
*   **Debris Removal:** Carefully remove all nesting materials and biological waste from beneath the array, ensuring no damage to roof membranes or mounting hardware.
*   **System Diagnostics:** Inspect the entire trunk cable and individual PV wire runs for insulation breaches, copper exposure, or mechanical damage. 
*   **Electrical Repairs:**
    *   Replace damaged sections of the trunk cable utilizing manufacturer-approved splice kits or cable replacements to restore AC voltage to the four identified MIs.
    *   Repair or replace compromised PV wire leads using appropriate heat-shrink, waterproof butt connectors or factory-compatible cabling.
    *   Perform continuity and insulation resistance (Megger) testing on all repaired circuits to ensure system integrity.
*   **Pest Mitigation:** Install high-grade, UV-stabilized stainless steel critter guard (mesh) around the entire perimeter of the array. Secure with UV-rated mechanical clips that do not require drilling into the modules or racking.
*   **Commissioning:** Restore power to the array, verify ACV output at the affected MIs, and confirm full system monitoring communication.

**3. Safety Considerations**
*   **Hazardous Energy:** All electrical work must be performed by a qualified electrician. LOTO protocols are mandatory until repairs are verified.
*   **Fall Protection:** All roof work must comply with OSHA standards, utilizing appropriate fall arrest or restraint systems.
*   **Biological Hazards:** Technicians must utilize appropriate PPE (gloves, respiratory protection) when removing nesting materials to mitigate exposure to zoonotic diseases or parasites.

**4. Methodology**
The approach will prioritize "isolate, inspect, repair, and protect." Repairs will be conducted using components compatible with the existing microinverter ecosystem to maintain warranty compliance. The installation of the critter guard will follow a mechanical-fastening approach that ensures long-term exclusion without compromising the array’s airflow or structural warranty. Final system checkout will include a visual inspection of all connections and a data-validation sweep to ensure full array performance.

Quote.scope_of_work:
### Scope of Work: PV System Remediation and Commissioning

**1. Objective**
Perform corrective maintenance to address thermal damage, restore system functionality, and ensure long-term operational integrity of the PV installation for the IQ Combiner. 

**2. Scope of Tasks**
*   **Component Replacement:**
    *   Decommission and remove the existing, thermally damaged Enphase IQ Combiner.
    *   Install a new IQ Combiner, ensuring proper mounting and structural integrity.
    *   Remove and replace the thermally damaged section of #8 AWG conductor between the PV generation disconnect and the combiner. Ensure all new wiring is properly rated, sized, and color-coded.
    *   Replace the failed Eaton 15A two-pole PV breaker within the existing electrical panel.
*   **Electrical Maintenance:**
    *   Inspect all existing electrical terminations within the scope area for signs of heat stress or oxidation.
    *   Perform a comprehensive re-torque of all electrical terminations (both new and existing connections) to manufacturer-specified torque settings using a calibrated torque wrench. 
*   **Commissioning and Verification:**
    *   Conduct full system commissioning, including polarity checks, voltage/amperage verification, and insulation resistance testing.
    *   Verify system synchronization and communication with the monitoring platform.
    *   Perform final production verification to ensure the system is operating within expected performance parameters.

**3. Safety Considerations**
*   **Hazard Mitigation:** All work must adhere to OSHA 1910 Subpart S and NFPA 70E standards. 
*   **Lockout/Tagout (LOTO):** Strict LOTO procedures must be implemented on all AC and DC disconnects prior to the commencement of any work.
*   **PPE:** Personnel must utilize appropriate Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), including arc-rated clothing, insulated gloves, and safety eyewear, as mandated by the site-specific Arc Flash analysis.
*   **Site Safety:** Maintain a clear work area and ensure all temporary wiring is managed to prevent tripping or inadvertent contact during the installation process.

**4. Methodology**
The technician will arrive on-site, verify the system status, and implement LOTO. Following equipment removal, the site will be prepped for new component installation. All hardware will be installed per manufacturer specifications and the NEC. Final verification will involve a step-by-step startup procedure, checking for proper voltage levels and thermal stability under load, followed by the submission of a documented post-maintenance commissioning report.

Quote.scope_of_work:
The objective of this project is to perform comprehensive electrical troubleshooting to remediate faults preventing AC voltage delivery to the battery storage system. Following diagnostics, the team will execute necessary hardware replacements of the damaged AC disconnect and blown fuses. 

**2. Methodology and Tasks**
*   **Diagnostics:** Conduct a full electrical system assessment, utilizing multimeters and insulation resistance testers to isolate the fault location between the utility interface and the battery system.
*   **Component Replacement:** Replace the damaged AC disconnect switch and all blown fuses identified during the diagnostic phase with components meeting original equipment manufacturer (OEM) specifications.
*   **Conductor Assessment:** Perform a visual and electrical inspection (continuity and insulation resistance/megger testing) of the existing underground conductors routed beneath the residence. 
    *   If conductors are verified as safe and serviceable, they will be retained and re-terminated.
    *   If conductor integrity is compromised (e.g., insulation breakdown or physical damage), the technician will document the findings with photographs and notify the client immediately. Replacement of these conductors will be addressed via a separate, mutually agreed-upon change order.
*   **System Testing:** Re-energize the circuit, verify proper AC voltage delivery to the battery inverter input, and conduct a final system functional test to confirm operational status.

**Scope of Work: Legacy PV System Audit, Commissioning, and Monitoring Integration**

**1. Objective**
The objective of this service is to perform a comprehensive physical audit of the existing rooftop photovoltaic array, map all components, integrate the system into a modern monitoring platform, and verify functional performance of all microinverters.

**2. Scope of Tasks**
*   **Physical Asset Audit:** Conduct a full onsite roof inspection to document all equipment. Capture and record manufacturer, model number, and serial number for every microinverter and PV module.
*   **Array Mapping:** Generate a detailed physical layout map correlating specific serial numbers to their precise geographic coordinates on the roof array.
*   **Connectivity & Monitoring:** Install and configure a compatible communication gateway. Integrate the legacy system into the specified monitoring portal to enable remote performance visibility.
*   **Functional Testing:** Perform a system-wide diagnostic check to verify operational status, communication link, and power production for every individual microinverter. Identify and document any offline or malfunctioning units.

**3. Safety Considerations**
*   **Fall Protection:** All personnel must strictly adhere to OSHA-compliant fall protection standards. Appropriate anchor points, harnesses, and lanyards are mandatory for any work performed on the roof surface.
*   **Electrical Safety:** All work must be performed in accordance with NFPA 70E standards. Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures must be implemented before inspecting or interacting with electrical enclosures, combiners, or disconnects.
*   **Site Environment:** A pre-work hazard assessment must be completed to identify potential roof structural concerns, environmental hazards, or site-specific obstructions.

**4. Methodology**
*   **Phased Approach:** The technician will first secure the site and establish appropriate work zones. 
*   **Data Collection:** Using a systematic grid-by-grid approach, the technician will photograph and log serial numbers, ensuring the final array map matches the physical installation.
*   **Integration:** Gateway installation will be performed at the existing electrical service point. Firmware updates will be pushed to the gateway to ensure compatibility with the legacy hardware.
*   **Verification:** Final testing will include a gateway "handshake" test to ensure data telemetry is successfully transmitting to the monitoring portal. A summary report including the array map, equipment list, and system performance status will be provided upon completion.

### Scope of Work: IQ Combiner 5c System Remediation and Electrical Repair

**1. Project Objective**
Removed and install new IQ Combiner 5c. The objective is to restore the system to full operational status by replacing compromised components, rectifying damaged conductors, and ensuring the PVC pathway meets original installation standards. 

**2. Scope of Tasks**
*   **Documentation:** Prior to any disassembly, provide high-resolution photo documentation of all thermal damage to establish a clear record of the incident’s origin. Thermally damaged IQ combiner and all breakers will be removed and mailed back for failure annalysis. 
*   **Component Replacement:** 
    *   Remove and replace the damaged IQ Combiner 5c with new IQ Combiner 5c..
    *   Replace (4) 20A breakers and one (1) 15A breaker affected by the event.
    *   Replace all damaged PVC conduit runs spanning from the System Controller to the IQ Combiner.
*   **Wiring/Conductor Remediation:** 
    *   Replace all compromised wiring associated with the IQ Combiner, including but not limited to: feeder conductors, neutral conductors, communication (bus) wiring, and Current Transformer (CT) leads.
*   **Testing and Commissioning:** 
    *   Perform continuity and insulation resistance testing on all new wire runs.
    *   Verify proper polarity and orientation of CTs.
    *   Recommission the IQ Combiner 5c in the Enphase Installer Toolkit to ensure proper communication with the System Controller and gateway.

**3. Safety Considerations**
*   **LOTO Procedures:** Strict adherence to Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) protocols is mandatory. All power sources, including utility grid and PV array (DC disconnects), must be isolated and verified de-energized before work commences.
*   **PPE Requirements:** Technicians must utilize appropriate Arc Flash PPE (as per NFPA 70E requirements) and insulated hand tools suitable for the voltage levels present.
*   **Site Hazards:** Inspect all surrounding electrical equipment for collateral heat damage or brittle insulation before energization.

**4. Methodology**
*   **System Shutdown:** Execute a full system shutdown and verify zero energy state.
*   **Deconstruction:** Carefully remove thermally compromised conduit and wiring, labeling all circuits to ensure correct termination in the replacement combiner.
*   **Reinstallation:** Install replacement PVC conduits according to NEC requirements, ensuring proper support and weatherproofing. Pull new conductors, maintaining appropriate wire gauge and color coding.
*   **Termination:** Terminate all feeders, neutrals, and communication lines to torque specifications provided by the manufacturer.
*   **Verification:** Perform a final visual inspection of all connections, verify system voltage/phasing, and confirm system reporting via the Enphase monitoring platform.

Quote.scope_of_work:
**Scope of Work: Communication Network Restoration and Battery Commissioning**

**Objective**
Restore site-wide monitoring connectivity by replacing faulty Zigbee Extender, re-establishing the Zigbee mesh network, and completing the final provisioning/commissioning of the battery storage system.

**Detailed Tasks**
1. **USB Extender Replacement:** Locate and de-commission failed USB extender units. Install new, compatible hardware and verify physical connection to the gateway/controller.
2. **Zigbee Network Restoration:** Perform a network-wide scan to identify communication gaps. Re-pair orphaned devices, optimize mesh topology, and confirm stable signal strength (RSSI) across all nodes.
3. **Battery Provisioning:** Execute final firmware updates, verify cell balancing, and complete the digital commissioning process to integrate the battery system with the site management platform.
4. **Validation:** Conduct end-to-end testing to ensure real-time telemetry data is accurately reporting to the monitoring dashboard.

**Safety Considerations**
* **Electrical Safety:** All work must be performed in accordance with NFPA 70E standards. Verify zero energy state before handling internal cabinet components. Use appropriate PPE, including insulated tools and arc-flash-rated gear where required.
* **Battery Handling:** Strictly adhere to manufacturer-specific safety protocols regarding high-voltage DC systems. Monitor for signs of thermal instability and ensure proper ventilation during testing.
* **Access Protocols:** Secure all enclosures upon completion to maintain NEMA/IP rating requirements.

**Approach and Methodology**
* **Diagnostic Phase:** Conduct initial continuity checks on communication lines and verify gateway heartbeat signals.
* **Execution Phase:** Implement a phased replacement approach to avoid cascading network failures. Use a systematic pairing process for Zigbee devices, starting from the gateway outwards.
* **Verification Phase:** Provide a post-service report detailing signal quality metrics, device online status, and battery state-of-health (SoH) diagnostics confirmed via the monitoring interface.

Quote.scope_of_work:
### Scope of Work: IQ Combiner 5c System Remediation and Electrical Repair

**1. Project Objective**
Perform a comprehensive site remediation following a thermal incident at the IQ Combiner 5c. The objective is to restore the system to full operational status by replacing compromised components, rectifying damaged conductors, and ensuring all electrical pathways meet original installation standards.

**2. Scope of Tasks**
*   **Documentation:** Prior to any disassembly, provide high-resolution photo documentation of all thermal damage to establish a clear record of the incident’s origin.
*   **Component Replacement:** 
    *   Remove and replace the damaged IQ Combiner 5c.
    *   Replace three (4) 20A breakers and one (1) 15A breaker affected by the event.
    *   Replace all damaged PVC conduit runs spanning from the System Controller to the IQ Combiner.
*   **Wiring/Conductor Remediation:** 
    *   Replace all compromised wiring associated with the IQ Combiner, including but not limited to: feeder conductors, neutral conductors, communication (bus) wiring, and Current Transformer (CT) leads.
*   **Testing and Commissioning:** 
    *   Perform continuity and insulation resistance testing on all new wire runs.
    *   Verify proper polarity and orientation of CTs.
    *   Recommission the IQ Combiner 5c in the Enphase Installer Toolkit to ensure proper communication with the System Controller and gateway.

**3. Safety Considerations**
*   **LOTO Procedures:** Strict adherence to Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) protocols is mandatory. All power sources, including utility grid and PV array (DC disconnects), must be isolated and verified de-energized before work commences.
*   **PPE Requirements:** Technicians must utilize appropriate Arc Flash PPE (as per NFPA 70E requirements) and insulated hand tools suitable for the voltage levels present.
*   **Site Hazards:** Inspect all surrounding electrical equipment for collateral heat damage or brittle insulation before energization.

**4. Methodology**
*   **System Shutdown:** Execute a full system shutdown and verify zero energy state.
*   **Deconstruction:** Carefully remove thermally compromised conduit and wiring, labeling all circuits to ensure correct termination in the replacement combiner.
*   **Reinstallation:** Install replacement PVC conduits according to NEC requirements, ensuring proper support and weatherproofing. Pull new conductors, maintaining appropriate wire gauge and color coding.
*   **Termination:** Terminate all feeders, neutrals, and communication lines to torque specifications provided by the manufacturer.
*   **Verification:** Perform a final visual inspection of all connections, verify system voltage/phasing, and confirm system reporting via the Enphase monitoring platform.

Quote.scope_of_work:
### Scope of Work: IQ Combiner 5c System Remediation and Electrical Repair

**1. Project Objective**
Perform a comprehensive site remediation following a thermal incident at the IQ Combiner 5c. The objective is to restore the system to full operational status by replacing compromised components, rectifying damaged conductors, and ensuring all electrical pathways meet original installation standards.

**2. Scope of Tasks**
*   **Documentation:** Prior to any disassembly, provide high-resolution photo documentation of all thermal damage to establish a clear record of the incident’s origin.
*   **Component Replacement:** 
    *   Remove and replace the damaged IQ Combiner 5c.
    *   Replace three (4) 20A breakers and one (1) 15A breaker affected by the event.
    *   Replace all damaged PVC conduit runs spanning from the System Controller to the IQ Combiner.
*   **Wiring/Conductor Remediation:** 
    *   Replace all compromised wiring associated with the IQ Combiner, including but not limited to: feeder conductors, neutral conductors, communication (bus) wiring, and Current Transformer (CT) leads.
*   **Testing and Commissioning:** 
    *   Perform continuity and insulation resistance testing on all new wire runs.
    *   Verify proper polarity and orientation of CTs.
    *   Recommission the IQ Combiner 5c in the Enphase Installer Toolkit to ensure proper communication with the System Controller and gateway.

**3. Safety Considerations**
*   **LOTO Procedures:** Strict adherence to Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) protocols is mandatory. All power sources, including utility grid and PV array (DC disconnects), must be isolated and verified de-energized before work commences.
*   **PPE Requirements:** Technicians must utilize appropriate Arc Flash PPE (as per NFPA 70E requirements) and insulated hand tools suitable for the voltage levels present.
*   **Site Hazards:** Inspect all surrounding electrical equipment for collateral heat damage or brittle insulation before energization.

**4. Methodology**
*   **System Shutdown:** Execute a full system shutdown and verify zero energy state.
*   **Deconstruction:** Carefully remove thermally compromised conduit and wiring, labeling all circuits to ensure correct termination in the replacement combiner.
*   **Reinstallation:** Install replacement PVC conduits according to NEC requirements, ensuring proper support and weatherproofing. Pull new conductors, maintaining appropriate wire gauge and color coding.
*   **Termination:** Terminate all feeders, neutrals, and communication lines to torque specifications provided by the manufacturer.
*   **Verification:** Perform a final visual inspection of all connections, verify system voltage/phasing, and confirm system reporting via the Enphase monitoring platform.

Quote.scope_of_work:
**Scope of Work: Wildlife Remediation and Electrical Repair – Site ID 3567740**

**Objective**
Resolve electrical faults caused by wildlife intrusion at the specified residence. By Repairing damaged branch wiring, and installing protective mitigation measures to prevent recurrence.

**Scope of Work**
1.  **Wildlife Removal & Site Preparation:**  Please note the removal of the wild life nesting areas will be need to be performed by a third party company before our technicians can proceed with site visit. Once confirmed completed, we can move forward with our process of resolving electrical fauts found in need of repair and installation of critter guard. 
2.  **Diagnostic Verification & Module Removal:** Carefully remove affected modules to expose the underlying Q-Cable and microinverter branch. Inspect the entire 9-microinverter string for insulation breaches, gnawed conductors, or damaged trunk cable connections.
3.  **Electrical Repair:**
    *   Perform localized repairs or replace the affected segment of the 11-port Q-Cable assembly.
    *   Utilize approved splice kits, Wago connectors, or section replacement as necessary to restore electrical integrity.
    *   Inspect the 20A IQ Combiner breaker; replace if evidence of heat fatigue or arc damage exists.
    *   Ensure all grounding and bonding connections remain intact and meet NEC standards.
4.  **System Restoration:** Reinstall modules, manage all wiring using UV-rated ties and clips to prevent future sagging or damage, and re-energize the affected branch.
5.  **Mitigation:** Install critter guard around the entire perimeter of the array to prevent future nesting or animal ingress.
6.  **Commissioning & Validation:** Perform a full system health check via Enphase Installer Toolkit (ITK). Verify stable communications, individual microinverter production, and correct system reporting for all 9 units in the branch.

**Safety Considerations**
*   **Fall Protection:** Due to the 12:12 (45-degree) roof pitch, technicians must utilize appropriate steep-roof fall protection systems, including safety harnesses, ropes, and anchors, at all times.
*   **Electrical Safety:** Ensure the affected 20A branch breaker is locked out/tagged out (LOTO) prior to beginning physical repairs. Confirm circuit isolation before handling conductors.
*   **Wildlife Protocol:** Technicians should maintain awareness of potential biological hazards associated with wildlife nests and utilize appropriate PPE during removal.

**Methodology**
The repair will be conducted by a two-person team to ensure safety compliance during high-pitch roof work. The technicians will systematically isolate the circuit, clear the obstruction, perform precision cable restoration, and verify system stability. All materials, including trunk cabling and critter guard, will be installed in accordance with manufacturer specifications and local building codes. Final site closure is contingent upon successful verification of system production and communication through the Envoy gateway.

**Scope of Work: Array Mapping and Communication Validation**

**Objective:**
Perform comprehensive array mapping and communication restoration for the microinverter systems at sites 4903810 and 4903826. The objective is to verify serial number placement against the physical layout and ensure 100% communication reliability for all units.

**Scope of Work:**
1.  **Site 4903810:** Perform array mapping for twenty-four (24) Enphase IQ8PLUS-72-M-US microinverters.
2.  **Site 4903826:** Perform array mapping for twenty-four (24) Enphase IQ8PLUS-72-M-US microinverters.
3.  **Physical Audit:** Physically verify each microinverter serial number relative to its corresponding module location on the roof array.
4.  **System Reconnection:** Perform a full power cycle/reconnection of the microinverter systems to clear communication faults.
5.  **Validation:** Utilize the Enphase Installer Toolkit (ITK) or equivalent software to confirm that all 48 total microinverters are reporting correctly to the Gateway/Envoy. 
6.  **Reporting:** Provide a final map update and ensure the system dashboard reflects active, fault-free communication for every unit.

**Methodology:**
*   Technicians will utilize site-specific layout drawings to cross-reference serial numbers.
*   Data collection will be performed via mobile application, ensuring real-time syncing with the Enphase Enlighten platform.
*   Troubleshooting will be conducted systematically, starting from the branch circuit level if communication persists as an issue after initial reconnection.

**Scope of Work: Legacy PV System Audit, Commissioning, and Monitoring Integration**

**1. Objective**
The objective of this service is to perform a comprehensive physical audit of the existing rooftop photovoltaic array, map all components, integrate the system into a modern monitoring platform, and verify functional performance of all microinverters.

**2. Scope of Tasks**
*   **Physical Asset Audit:** Conduct a full onsite roof inspection to document all equipment. Capture and record manufacturer, model number, and serial number for every microinverter and PV module.
*   **Array Mapping:** Generate a detailed physical layout map correlating specific serial numbers to their precise geographic coordinates on the roof array.
*   **Connectivity & Monitoring:** Install and configure a compatible communication gateway. Integrate the legacy system into the specified monitoring portal to enable remote performance visibility.
*   **Functional Testing:** Perform a system-wide diagnostic check to verify operational status, communication link, and power production for every individual microinverter. Identify and document any offline or malfunctioning units.

**3. Safety Considerations**
*   **Fall Protection:** All personnel must strictly adhere to OSHA-compliant fall protection standards. Appropriate anchor points, harnesses, and lanyards are mandatory for any work performed on the roof surface.
*   **Electrical Safety:** All work must be performed in accordance with NFPA 70E standards. Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures must be implemented before inspecting or interacting with electrical enclosures, combiners, or disconnects.
*   **Site Environment:** A pre-work hazard assessment must be completed to identify potential roof structural concerns, environmental hazards, or site-specific obstructions.

**4. Methodology**
*   **Phased Approach:** The technician will first secure the site and establish appropriate work zones. 
*   **Data Collection:** Using a systematic grid-by-grid approach, the technician will photograph and log serial numbers, ensuring the final array map matches the physical installation.
*   **Integration:** Gateway installation will be performed at the existing electrical service point. Firmware updates will be pushed to the gateway to ensure compatibility with the legacy hardware.
*   **Verification:** Final testing will include a gateway "handshake" test to ensure data telemetry is successfully transmitting to the monitoring portal. A summary report including the array map, equipment list, and system performance status will be provided upon completion.

**Scope of Work: Gateway ENV4 PCBA Replacement**

**Objective**
To restore system communication and reporting by replacing the failed Envoy (ENV4) Printed Circuit Board Assembly (PCBA). The current unit has been diagnosed with a persistent provisioning failure and a recurring health check fault, deemed non-repairable under warranty.

*   **Static Discharge:** Handle the replacement PCBA using proper ESD (Electrostatic Discharge) mitigation techniques to prevent damage to sensitive electronic components.
*   **Site Access:** All work must be performed in accordance with local electrical codes and site-specific safety protocols. 

**Methodology**
The technician will arrive on-site, verify the reported fault status, and perform the hardware swap using manufacturer-approved procedures. Post-installation, the technician will perform a soft-reset and network re-provisioning. The job is considered complete only upon receipt of a confirmed successful health check and validated reporting status in the monitoring portal.

**Scope of Work: Enphase M250 Microinverter Replacement**

**1. Project Objective**
Replace one failed Enphase M250 microinverter identified as non-functional (no AC voltage output) to restore full array performance.

**2. Scope of Tasks**
*   **Site Preparation:** Perform a field safety assessment. Access the array at the identified location per site layout.
*   **Removal:** Disconnect the associated PV module from the failed microinverter. Disconnect the microinverter from the AC trunk cable. Remove the failed unit from the racking system.
*   **Installation:** Mount the replacement Enphase M250 unit to the racking system. Connect the DC leads from the PV module and the AC connector to the trunk cable.
*   **System Integration:** Update the Envoy/Enphase Installer Toolkit to reflect the new serial number (SN) and initiate the replacement process in the Enlighten monitoring platform.
*   **Verification:** Confirm that the Envoy successfully recognizes the new unit. Verify the unit is communicating and reporting AC production.
*   **Post-Installation Check:** Ensure all connections are secure, cable management is restored to original specifications, and the PV module is properly re-secured to the racking.

**3. Safety Considerations**
*   **Electrical Hazard:** Technicians must utilize appropriate PPE, including insulated gloves and voltage-rated tools. All work must follow LOTO (Lockout/Tagout) procedures on the branch circuit breaker prior to handling AC connectors.
*   **Fall Protection:** If performing work on sloped or elevated surfaces, technicians must utilize fall protection equipment (harnesses and lanyards) in accordance with OSHA standards.
*   **DC Safety:** Treat PV modules as live; exercise caution when disconnecting DC leads, as they remain energized in the presence of sunlight.

**4. Methodology**
The technician will utilize a systematic approach: isolate the branch circuit, perform the hardware swap, utilize the Enphase Installer Toolkit for digital commissioning, and conduct a data-validated functional test. Success is defined by the unit reporting normal operational status and production data within the Enphase Enlighten monitoring portal.

*   **Commissioning & Software:** Re-energize the system, perform firmware updates as required to ensure version compatibility between the new module and the existing battery management system (BMS), and initiate the automated system handshake/discovery process.
*   **Validation:** Conduct full functional testing, including BMS communication verification, state-of-charge (SoC) calibration, and system-level performance validation to ensure the unit is operational and error-free.

**3. Safety Considerations**
*   **PPE:** Personnel must utilize appropriate Arc Flash Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), insulated tools, and voltage-rated gloves as required by NFPA 70E.
*   **Isolation:** Strict adherence to Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures is mandatory for all AC and DC disconnects prior to any service work.
*   **Handling:** Batteries must be handled using proper lifting equipment to prevent mechanical damage or injury. Defective units must be packaged per the Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA) instructions provided by the manufacturer.

**4. Methodology**
*   **Pre-Service:** Review all fault logs prior to arrival. Verify that the replacement battery is on-site and authorized for installation.
*   **Execution:** Work will be performed sequentially—isolation, physical swap, firmware verification, and systematic testing—ensuring that all modules are operating within thermal and electrical tolerances.
*   **Post-Service:** Provide a final commissioning report confirming the clearing of all fault codes, successful battery synchronization, and overall system operational stability.

**Scope of Work: Post-Grid Event Site Assessment and Diagnostic Inspection**

**1. Objective**
Conduct a comprehensive onsite inspection and diagnostic evaluation of the solar photovoltaic (PV) system following a recorded grid event. The objective is to identify potential damage to system components, verify equipment integrity, and restore the system to optimal operational status.

**2. Scope of Tasks**
*   **Visual Inspection:** Conduct a perimeter and component-level walkthrough to identify signs of surge damage, electrical arcing, localized heating, or physical damage to mounting structures and balance-of-system (BOS) components.
*   **Electrical Testing:** 
    *   Perform insulation resistance (Megger) testing on DC home-run wiring to ensure cable integrity.
    *   Verify string voltages and currents to identify potential module damage or bypass diode failure.
    *   Test AC protection devices (breakers, fuses, surge suppression devices) for continuity and evidence of thermal distress.
*   **Communication & Logic Audit:** Inspect inverter communication boards, data loggers, and control circuitry for fault codes or non-responsive hardware resulting from potential voltage transients.
*   **Data Analysis:** Compare pre-event and post-event system telemetry to identify performance degradation or anomalies not visible during physical inspection.

**3. Safety Considerations**
*   **Lockout/Tagout (LOTO):** All personnel must adhere to strict LOTO procedures prior to opening enclosures or accessing energized components.
*   **PPE Requirements:** Technicians must utilize appropriate arc-rated (AR) clothing, high-voltage insulated gloves, and arc-flash face shields consistent with the facility’s NFPA 70E risk assessment.
*   **Voltage Verification:** Verify zero-energy state using a calibrated, category-rated multimeter prior to manual handling of equipment.
*   **Environmental Hazards:** Assessment of external components shall be deferred if adverse weather conditions present a slip, trip, or fall risk.

**4. Methodology**
*   **Phase I: Data Gathering:** Review inverter event logs, utility smart-meter reports, and site monitoring data to isolate the timing and nature of the grid anomaly.
*   **Phase II: Site Inspection:** Execute a methodical "top-down" approach, starting with the Point of Interconnection (POI), moving through the combiner boxes/inverters, and concluding at the PV array.
*   **Phase III: Remediation & Reporting:** Replace damaged surge protection devices or blown fuses as necessary. Provide a detailed summary report including photographic evidence of findings, test results, and recommendations for permanent repairs or further component replacement if required.

Quote.scope_of_work:
### Scope of Work: IQ Combiner 5c System Remediation and Electrical Repair

**1. Project Objective**
Perform a comprehensive site remediation following a thermal incident at the IQ Combiner 5c. The objective is to restore the system to full operational status by replacing compromised components, rectifying damaged conductors, and ensuring all electrical pathways meet original installation standards.

**2. Scope of Tasks**
*   **Documentation:** Prior to any disassembly, provide high-resolution photo documentation of all thermal damage to establish a clear record of the incident’s origin.
*   **Component Replacement:** 
    *   Remove and replace the damaged IQ Combiner 5c.
    *   Replace three (4) 20A breakers and one (1) 15A breaker affected by the event.
    *   Replace all damaged PVC conduit runs spanning from the System Controller to the IQ Combiner.
*   **Wiring/Conductor Remediation:** 
    *   Replace all compromised wiring associated with the IQ Combiner, including but not limited to: feeder conductors, neutral conductors, communication (bus) wiring, and Current Transformer (CT) leads.
*   **Testing and Commissioning:** 
    *   Perform continuity and insulation resistance testing on all new wire runs.
    *   Verify proper polarity and orientation of CTs.
    *   Recommission the IQ Combiner 5c in the Enphase Installer Toolkit to ensure proper communication with the System Controller and gateway.

**3. Safety Considerations**
*   **LOTO Procedures:** Strict adherence to Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) protocols is mandatory. All power sources, including utility grid and PV array (DC disconnects), must be isolated and verified de-energized before work commences.
*   **PPE Requirements:** Technicians must utilize appropriate Arc Flash PPE (as per NFPA 70E requirements) and insulated hand tools suitable for the voltage levels present.
*   **Site Hazards:** Inspect all surrounding electrical equipment for collateral heat damage or brittle insulation before energization.

**4. Methodology**
*   **System Shutdown:** Execute a full system shutdown and verify zero energy state.
*   **Deconstruction:** Carefully remove thermally compromised conduit and wiring, labeling all circuits to ensure correct termination in the replacement combiner.
*   **Reinstallation:** Install replacement PVC conduits according to NEC requirements, ensuring proper support and weatherproofing. Pull new conductors, maintaining appropriate wire gauge and color coding.
*   **Termination:** Terminate all feeders, neutrals, and communication lines to torque specifications provided by the manufacturer.
*   **Verification:** Perform a final visual inspection of all connections, verify system voltage/phasing, and confirm system reporting via the Enphase monitoring platform.

*   **Commissioning & Software:** Re-energize the system, perform firmware updates as required to ensure version compatibility between the new module and the existing battery management system (BMS), and initiate the automated system handshake/discovery process.
*   **Validation:** Conduct full functional testing, including BMS communication verification, state-of-charge (SoC) calibration, and system-level performance validation to ensure the unit is operational and error-free.

**3. Safety Considerations**
*   **PPE:** Personnel must utilize appropriate Arc Flash Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), insulated tools, and voltage-rated gloves as required by NFPA 70E.
*   **Isolation:** Strict adherence to Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures is mandatory for all AC and DC disconnects prior to any service work.
*   **Handling:** Batteries must be handled using proper lifting equipment to prevent mechanical damage or injury. Defective units must be packaged per the Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA) instructions provided by the manufacturer.

**4. Methodology**
*   **Pre-Service:** Review all fault logs prior to arrival. Verify that the replacement battery is on-site and authorized for installation.
*   **Execution:** Work will be performed sequentially—isolation, physical swap, firmware verification, and systematic testing—ensuring that all modules are operating within thermal and electrical tolerances.

Quote.scope_of_work:
**Scope of Work: PV Branch Circuit Remediation and Critter Damage Repair**

**Objective**
The objective of this service visit is to restore the integrity and functionality of the PV branch circuit compromised by wildlife-related damage. The onsite team will consist of two technicians to ensure safety, efficiency, and compliance with electrical standards.

**Scope of Work**
*   **Site Preparation and Safety:** Perform a comprehensive Job Hazard Analysis (JHA) upon arrival. Verify the affected branch circuit breaker is locked out/tagged out (LOTO) in the "OFF" position. Utilize proper Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) for electrical hazards and potential wildlife debris.
*   **Damage Investigation:** Conduct a systematic inspection of the affected branch circuit, including all PV modules, home-run wiring, and trunk cabling. Identify the extent of squirrel-induced insulation stripping, conductor damage, and connector compromise.
*   **Mitigation and Debris Removal:** Remove all nesting materials, fecal matter, and critter-related obstructions from the array area. Clear debris from wire management pathways to prevent recurring damage.
*   **Repairs and Component Replacement:** Replace damaged segments of trunk cabling, branch connectors, and/or module leads as necessary. All repairs must utilize manufacturer-approved components and weather-rated splicing or termination methods to maintain original system integrity and environmental sealing.
*   **System Testing and Commissioning:**
    *   Perform continuity and insulation resistance (Megger) testing on the repaired circuit to ensure electrical safety.
    *   Verify correct polarity and voltage readings at the combiner box/inverter input before re-energizing the breaker.
    *   Perform a system-wide test to ensure all modules on the circuit are communicating and producing within expected parameters.
*   **Verification:** Monitor inverter production data post-repair to confirm the return of the affected circuit to nominal performance levels. Clear all fault codes from the monitoring platform.

**Methodology**
The project will be executed following National Electrical Code (NEC) guidelines and site-specific safety protocols. All work will be performed during morning hours to maximize environmental conditions for the technicians and minimize potential heat-related fatigue. Upon completion, technicians will provide a summary report documenting the nature of the damage, repairs performed, and final system verification status.

**Scope of Work: Solar Array Repair and Mitigation (Location 7478)**

**1. Project Objective**
Provide all necessary labor, materials, equipment, and travel to remediate rodent-related damage at microinverter location ending 7478. The scope includes localized component replacement and the installation of a perimeter critter guard to prevent recurring electrical faults.

**2. Scope of Services**
*   **Component Replacement:** Remove and replace the damaged SunPower SPR-X22-370-E-AC AC module. Replace the damaged trunk cable head and install new, manufacturer-approved field-wireable connectors.
*   **System Restoration:** Inspect all affected wiring within the localized area. Re-terminate and secure all connections to ensure electrical continuity and adherence to NEC standards. Test the circuit post-repair to verify proper microinverter communication and power output.
*   **Preventative Mitigation:** Install approximately 300 linear feet of high-durability, UV-resistant solar critter guard (mesh) around the array perimeter. Secure the mesh using non-penetrating mounting clips to ensure a tight seal against the roof surface, effectively blocking entry points for rodents and nesting wildlife.

**3. Safety Considerations**
*   **Electrical Hazards:** All work shall be performed in accordance with NFPA 70E. The system must be properly isolated and locked out/tagged out (LOTO) prior to initiating repairs. Technicians must verify zero energy state before handling AC/DC conductors.
*   **Fall Protection:** All roof access and work must comply with OSHA 1926.501 (Fall Protection). Technicians are required to utilize certified anchor points and personal fall arrest systems (PFAS) where applicable.
*   **PPE:** Personnel shall wear appropriate personal protective equipment, including arc-rated clothing, insulated gloves, and safety glasses, as necessitated by the specific site conditions.

**4. Methodology**
*   **Site Preparation:** Conduct a pre-work site assessment to verify structural integrity and identify potential hazards.
*   **Repair Phase:** Carefully de-energize the specific branch circuit, replace damaged hardware, and restore electrical connectivity. Perform insulation resistance testing (megger) as required to confirm cable integrity.
*   **Mitigation Phase:** Install the critter guard in continuous sections, ensuring consistent contact with the roof surface. Confirm that the guard does not impede necessary natural ventilation for the modules.
*   **Quality Control:** Perform a final visual inspection of all repairs and a functional verification of the replaced module via the monitoring portal. Ensure the work area is cleared of all debris, wire scraps, and packaging materials.

Quote.scope_of_work:
**Scope of Work: Gateway Communication Infrastructure Upgrade**

**Objective**
Relocate the existing standalone PV Gateway to a new dedicated power source fed from the PV breaker panel to resolve ongoing communication instability and restore full system monitoring visibility.

**Methodology**
1. **Site Preparation and Decommissioning:** De-energize the existing Gateway unit and perform a controlled disconnection from the current power source.
2. **Dedicated Circuit Installation:** Install a new dedicated receptacle fed directly from the PV breaker panel. All electrical work shall be performed in accordance with the National Electrical Code (NEC) and local jurisdiction requirements.
3. **Enclosure Installation:** Mount a 12"x12" NEMA-rated outdoor enclosure at the designated location to protect the Gateway and receptacle components from environmental exposure.
4. **Relocation and Commissioning:** Secure the Gateway within the new enclosure, complete the final wiring connections to the dedicated circuit, and power on the device.
5. **System Verification:** Perform a full diagnostic handshake to confirm signal stability and verify that all PV modules are correctly reporting to the monitoring platform.

**Safety Considerations**
* **Electrical Safety:** All work must be performed by a qualified technician using appropriate Personal Protective Equipment (PPE). Verify zero-energy states using a calibrated multimeter prior to handling conductors.
* **Lockout/Tagout (LOTO):** Strict adherence to LOTO procedures is required when interfacing with the PV breaker panel to prevent accidental re-energization during installation.
* **Environmental Integrity:** Ensure all conduit entries and enclosure penetrations are properly sealed with weatherproof fittings/hubs to maintain the NEMA rating of the enclosure and prevent moisture ingress.
* **Site Awareness:** As a single-story residential site, maintain proper workspace clearances around the new installation area to ensure safe access for future maintenance.

Quote.scope_of_work:
**Scope of Work: Microinverter Replacement and System Recommissioning**

**1. Project Objective**
Perform corrective maintenance to restore full functionality to the specified photovoltaic (PV) array by replacing a failed microinverter, updating site documentation, and verifying system performance.

**2. Scope of Tasks**
*   **Site Mobilization:** Travel to the project site, perform a pre-task safety briefing, and establish a secure work zone.
*   **Access and Preparation:** Safely access the metal-roof shop building using approved fall protection equipment. Perform necessary physical maneuvers to locate the specific module associated with the failed microinverter.
*   **Hardware Replacement:** De-energize the affected branch circuit. Remove the PV module, disconnect and replace the failed microinverter with an identical or compatible unit, and reinstall the PV module, ensuring all cabling is properly routed and secured to prevent mechanical stress or abrasion.
*   **Documentation and Configuration:** Update the site’s physical array map to reflect the new serial number. Configure the monitoring platform to pair the new microinverter with the existing gateway.
*   **Testing and Recommissioning:** Perform a full system check to confirm communication stability with the gateway. Verify that the replaced unit is generating power and reporting performance data accurately.
*   **Closeout:** Remove all debris, restore the work area to its original condition, and provide a post-maintenance report confirming system health and successful recommissioning.

**3. Safety Considerations**
*   **Fall Protection:** All personnel accessing the metal roof must utilize appropriate fall arrest or restraint systems in accordance with OSHA standards. Metal roofs present slip hazards, particularly if damp; work must be suspended during inclement weather.
*   **Electrical Safety:** All work must be performed in accordance with NFPA 70E. Verify zero-energy state via multi-meter testing prior to commencing hardware replacement. Utilize appropriate arc-flash PPE as required.
*   **General Site Safety:** Adherence to site-specific safety protocols and personal protective equipment (PPE) requirements, including hard hats and high-visibility vests where required.

**4. Methodology**
*   **Technical Approach:** Replacement will follow manufacturer-recommended installation procedures to maintain warranty integrity and ensure NEC-compliant connections.
*   **Quality Assurance:** Post-replacement validation will include a "live" system check via the manufacturer's monitoring portal to ensure data acquisition and reporting are fully synchronized before site departure.

Quote.scope_of_work:
### Scope of Work for PLC Communication Restoration 

#### 1. Project Overview  
The primary objective is to restore Power Line Communication (PLC) reliability and monitoring visibility in a photovoltaic system. The system is currently producing energy, but has lost module-level communications following a utility outage on March 5, 2025. Previous recovery attempts, including Envoy swaps, RF corrections, and ferrite installations, have failed.

#### 2. Specific Tasks  
- **Install PV Subpanel**:  
  Construct a dedicated PV subpanel to isolate the photovoltaic circuits from the main service panel.
  
- **Reroute PV Circuits**:  
  Reroute three existing PV circuits to the newly installed subpanel to minimize interference.
  
- **Install Feeder & Ferrites**:  
  Install appropriate feeder conductors and ferrite filters to mitigate signal degradation caused by impedance and noise.
  
- **Install Envoy-S & CTs**:  
  Integrate the Envoy-S communication device with current transformers (CTs) to facilitate data acquisition and monitoring.
  
- **Commissioning & PLC Validation**:  
  Conduct a comprehensive commissioning process including the validation of PLC capabilities and signal strength.

- **Documentation & Testing**:  
  Thoroughly document the installation process and test the system to ensure reliability and performance metrics are met.

#### 3. Safety Considerations  
- Adhere to all local and national electrical safety codes and standards.
- Conduct lockout/tagout (LOTO) procedures during installation to ensure safety when working on electrical components.
- Utilize personal protective equipment (PPE) including gloves, goggles, and insulated tools.
- Ensure the work area is clear of hazards and barriers are in place to restrict access during installation.

#### 4. Expected Approach/Methodology  
- **Pre-Installation Survey**:  
  Assess the existing electrical architecture to identify optimal routing for the new subpanel and circuits.
  
- **Installation Procedure**:  
  Sequentially install the subpanel, reroute circuits, and integrate ferrite filters, ensuring minimal disruption to ongoing energy production.

- **Commissioning Process**:  
  Upon installation completion, execute the commissioning checklist, focusing on gateway validation, PLC quality, microinverter recovery, and CT verification.

- **Verification Steps**:  
  - Validate the Envoy is online and reporting accurately, ensuring firmware is current and device scan completes.
  - Measure signal strength and noise floor for each branch, checking for any phase coupling issues.
  - Confirm that the device count matches expected outputs, the array map populates correctly, and historical data backfill initiates.
  - Check that production aligns with inverter output and consumption polarity is correct.

#### 5. Outcome  
This scope aims to improve PLC reliability and enhance monitoring capabilities, with actual restoration of module-level monitoring contingent upon the successful commissioning and validation process.

Quote.scope_of_work:
**Scope of Work: Gateway Board Relocation and Enclosure Installation**

**Objective**
To remediate the improper installation of the system gateway board currently situated within the base of the system controller. The board shall be relocated to a dedicated, weather-rated, and secure enclosure to ensure compliance with manufacturer specifications, improve thermal management, and provide physical protection.

**Scope of Work**
1.  **De-energization:** Perform a complete lockout/tagout (LOTO) procedure on all AC and DC sources connected to the system controller to ensure a zero-energy state.
2.  **Removal:** Carefully disconnect all communication cables and power leads from the existing gateway board. Remove the board from the bottom of the system controller housing.
3.  **Enclosure Installation:** Install a NEMA-rated enclosure adjacent to the system controller. The enclosure must be mounted securely to the mounting surface according to site requirements and manufacturer guidelines.
4.  **Hardware Relocation:** Mount the gateway board within the new enclosure using non-conductive standoffs to ensure proper clearance and thermal dissipation.
5.  **Wiring and Termination:** Extend or reroute communication and power wiring as necessary. All field-installed wiring shall be landed according to the original schematic, ensuring proper strain relief and aesthetic cable management.
6.  **Verification:** Conduct a visual inspection of all connections to ensure no short circuits or loose terminations. Perform a system startup, confirm communication link stability, and verify that the gateway is reporting correctly to the monitoring platform.

**Safety Considerations**
*   **Electrical Hazard:** All work must be performed by a qualified electrician in accordance with NFPA 70 (NEC) and OSHA 29 CFR 1910.333.
*   **LOTO:** Strict adherence to LOTO protocols is mandatory to prevent accidental re-energization during the relocation process.
*   **Static Sensitivity:** Standard ESD (Electrostatic Discharge) mitigation practices must be followed while handling the gateway board to prevent component damage.

**Methodology**
The project will be executed by first verifying the current wiring configuration, documenting all lead connections, performing a safe shutdown, and executing the physical relocation. All wiring will be routed through appropriate conduit or cable glands to maintain the NEMA rating of the new enclosure. Final commissioning will include a functional test of the communication link to ensure system performance remains unaffected by the relocation.

**Scope of Work: Current Transformer (CT) Installation and Conduit Infrastructure**

**Objective**
Furnish and install a new conduit pathway and four (4) Current Transformer (CT) sensors to facilitate energy monitoring integration at the main service panel.

**Methodology**
1. **Conduit Installation:** Install approximately 5 linear feet of new code-compliant conduit (EMT or flexible non-metallic tubing, as site conditions dictate) from the existing solar combiner/disconnect to the main service panel. Ensure proper anchoring and securement per NEC requirements.
2. **Wiring and Integration:** Fish CT communication wiring through the newly installed conduit pathway. Terminate CTs onto the main service conductors within the main service panel, ensuring proper orientation and polarity.
3. **System Commissioning:** Connect CT leads to the solar monitoring hardware. Verify communication and data accuracy via the monitoring platform to ensure valid readings.
4. **Site Restoration:** Patch, seal, and fire-stop any wall penetrations resulting from the new conduit run to maintain the integrity of the building envelope.

**Safety Considerations**
* **Energized Equipment:** All work within the main service panel must be performed by a qualified electrician. Live-front hazards exist; appropriate arc-flash PPE (Level 2 minimum), insulated tools, and adherence to NFPA 70E safety protocols are mandatory.
* **Lockout/Tagout (LOTO):** Solar disconnects must be placed in the "OFF" position and locked/tagged out prior to any work within the combiner or disconnect enclosure.
* **Conduit Routing:** Ensure all new conduit routing maintains required clearances from existing gas lines, plumbing, and structural members.
* **Code Compliance:** All installations shall be performed in strict accordance with the current edition of the National Electrical Code (NEC) and local AHJ requirements.

**Scope of Work: Solar Circuit Wiring Remediation and System Inspection**

**1. Objective**
Remove and replace compromised circuit wiring for Line 1 and Line 2 between the IQ Combiner box and the rooftop junction box to restore system integrity and performance.

**2. Scope of Tasks**
*   **Decommissioning:** Perform safe lockout/tagout (LOTO) procedures on the solar PV system. Disconnect existing Line 1 and Line 2 conductors at the IQ Combiner box and the designated rooftop junction box. Remove all damaged or compromised cabling from the conduit run.
*   **Reinstallation:** Install new, code-compliant PV wire (Line 1 and Line 2) over the approximate 35-foot span. Ensure all conductors are properly terminated, torque-verified per manufacturer specifications, and labeled for identification.
*   **System Inspection:** Conduct a comprehensive audit of the circuit path and associated equipment. Perform a physical inspection of all electrical connections, terminal blocks, and conduit fittings for evidence of arcing, heat stress, or moisture intrusion.
*   **Water Intrusion Mitigation:** Inspect all junction box seals, conduit entries, and cable glands. Apply industrial-grade sealant or replace compromised weather-proofing components as necessary to prevent future water ingress.

**3. Safety and Methodology**
*   **Safety Protocols:** All work must be performed in accordance with NFPA 70 (National Electrical Code), OSHA 1910 Subpart S (Electrical Safety), and site-specific safety plans. Technicians shall utilize appropriate Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), including arc-rated clothing and insulated tools.
*   **LOTO:** Strict adherence to Lockout/Tagout procedures is mandatory before beginning any electrical work.
*   **Verification:** Upon completion, perform polarity checks, open-circuit voltage (VOC) testing, and continuity testing to verify the circuit is operating within design parameters. 
*   **Quality Control:** All wiring shall be routed to prevent mechanical strain, secured with approved fasteners, and verified for proper grounding and bonding continuity.

**Scope of Work: Gateway Communication Infrastructure Upgrade**

**Objective**
Relocate the existing standalone PV Gateway to a new dedicated power source fed from the PV breaker panel to resolve ongoing communication instability and restore full system monitoring visibility.

**Methodology**
1. **Site Preparation and Decommissioning:** De-energize the existing Gateway unit and perform a controlled disconnection from the current power source.
2. **Dedicated Circuit Installation:** Install a new dedicated receptacle fed directly from the PV breaker panel. All electrical work shall be performed in accordance with the National Electrical Code (NEC) and local jurisdiction requirements.
3. **Enclosure Installation:** Mount a 12"x12" NEMA-rated outdoor enclosure at the designated location to protect the Gateway and receptacle components from environmental exposure.
4. **Relocation and Commissioning:** Secure the Gateway within the new enclosure, complete the final wiring connections to the dedicated circuit, and power on the device.
5. **System Verification:** Perform a full diagnostic handshake to confirm signal stability and verify that all PV modules are correctly reporting to the monitoring platform.

**Safety Considerations**
* **Electrical Safety:** All work must be performed by a qualified technician using appropriate Personal Protective Equipment (PPE). Verify zero-energy states using a calibrated multimeter prior to handling conductors.
* **Lockout/Tagout (LOTO):** Strict adherence to LOTO procedures is required when interfacing with the PV breaker panel to prevent accidental re-energization during installation.
* **Environmental Integrity:** Ensure all conduit entries and enclosure penetrations are properly sealed with weatherproof fittings/hubs to maintain the NEMA rating of the enclosure and prevent moisture ingress.
* **Site Awareness:** As a single-story residential site, maintain proper workspace clearances around the new installation area to ensure safe access for future maintenance.

Scope of Work – Enphase LPUP (Legacy Product Upgrade Program) Upgrade
 Customer: Lance Lipton
 Site Address: 1680 East Strasburg Road, West Chester, PA 19380

Project Overview

This project consists of upgrading the existing legacy Enphase microinverter system under the Enphase Legacy Product Upgrade Program (LPUP). The work will include the removal and replacement of failed or unsupported legacy microinverters, installation of a new Enphase communications and monitoring system, replacement of associated branch circuit cabling as required, and commissioning of the upgraded system.

Scope of Services
1. Site Preparation and Safety
Perform site assessment and establish safe work area.
De-energize the solar PV system in accordance with safety procedures.
Verify existing system configuration and equipment quantities.
2. Removal of Existing Equipment
Remove and properly dispose of existing legacy microinverters designated for replacement.
Remove existing communications equipment and associated components as required.
Remove and replace DC/AC cabling where necessary to support the upgraded system.
3. Installation of New Equipment

Install the following Enphase equipment supplied through the LPUP program:

Quantity	Description16	Enphase IQ7PD-72 Microinverters
1	Enphase IQ Combiner 5 HDK
21 Drops	IQ Q-Cable Single Drop (Landscape Configuration)
1 Pack	Q Cable Sealing Caps
1 Pack	IQ Terminator Caps
1 Pack	IQ Disconnect Tools
1 Pack	Q Cable Rail Mount Clips
4. System Wiring and Integration
Install and secure new Q-Cable infrastructure.
Connect and commission all replacement IQ7PD microinverters.
Install and wire the IQ Combiner 5 HDK.
Verify proper grounding and electrical connections.
Install cable management components and secure wiring in accordance with applicable codes and manufacturer requirements.
5. Monitoring and Commissioning
Configure and activate Enphase monitoring and communications.
Verify communication between all installed microinverters and the gateway/combiner.
Commission the system through Enphase monitoring platforms.
Confirm production reporting and proper system operation.
6. Testing and Verification
Perform operational testing of the upgraded solar PV system.
Validate production from all newly installed microinverters.
Confirm system functionality and monitoring visibility.
Document final installation and commissioning results.

2.  **Diagnostic Verification & Module Removal:** Carefully remove affected modules to expose the underlying Q-Cable and microinverter branch. Inspect the entire 9-microinverter string for insulation breaches, gnawed conductors, or damaged trunk cable connections.
3.  **Electrical Repair:**
    *   Perform localized repairs or replace the affected segment of the 11-port Q-Cable assembly.
    *   Utilize approved splice kits, Wago connectors, or section replacement as necessary to restore electrical integrity.
    *   Inspect the 20A IQ Combiner breaker; replace if evidence of heat fatigue or arc damage exists.
    *   Ensure all grounding and bonding connections remain intact and meet NEC standards.
4.  **System Restoration:** Reinstall modules, manage all wiring using UV-rated ties and clips to prevent future sagging or damage, and re-energize the affected branch.
5.  **Mitigation:** Install critter guard around the entire perimeter of the array to prevent future nesting or animal ingress.
6.  **Commissioning & Validation:** Perform a full system health check via Enphase Installer Toolkit (ITK). Verify stable communications, individual microinverter production, and correct system reporting for all 9 units in the branch.

**Safety Considerations**
*   **Fall Protection:** Due to the 12:12 (45-degree) roof pitch, technicians must utilize appropriate steep-roof fall protection systems, including safety harnesses, ropes, and anchors, at all times.
*   **Electrical Safety:** Ensure the affected 20A branch breaker is locked out/tagged out (LOTO) prior to beginning physical repairs. Confirm circuit isolation before handling conductors.
*   **Wildlife Protocol:** Technicians should maintain awareness of potential biological hazards associated with wildlife nests and utilize appropriate PPE during removal.

**Methodology**
The repair will be conducted by a two-person team to ensure safety compliance during high-pitch roof work. The technicians will systematically isolate the circuit, clear the obstruction, perform precision cable restoration, and verify system stability. All materials, including trunk cabling and critter guard, will be installed in accordance with manufacturer specifications and local building codes. Final site closure is contingent upon successful verification of system production and communication through the Envoy gateway.
