Quote.scope_of_work:
**Scope of Work for Electrical/Solar Maintenance and Service**

**Project Title:** Panel and Trunk Head Replacement

**1. Objective:**
To replace a faulty solar panel and trunk head, ensuring optimal performance and compliance with safety standards.

**2. Tasks:**

a. **Panel Replacement:**
   - Carefully remove the damaged solar panel from its mounting structure.
   - Inspect the surrounding area for potential damage or corrosion.
   - Install the new solar panel securely, ensuring proper alignment and stability.
   - Connect the new panel to the existing electrical system following manufacturer specifications.

b. **Terminator Cap Installation:**
   - Obtain and install a new terminator cap on the solar panel to prevent moisture ingress and ensure safe electrical connections.

c. **Trunk Head Replacement:**
   - Safely remove the damaged trunk head that has been compromised by chewing.
   - Procure a new trunk head with two male and two female connectors.
   - Install the new trunk head in accordance with electrical standards, ensuring all connections are secure and properly insulated.

**3. Safety Considerations:**
- Conduct a pre-work safety assessment to identify potential hazards, including electrical shock and fall risks.
- Utilize appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE), including gloves, safety glasses, and hard hats.
- Ensure all electrical power to the area is shut off before commencing work.
- Follow lockout/tagout (LOTO) procedures to prevent accidental re-energization of the system during maintenance.

**4. Methodology:**
- Begin with a site survey to evaluate existing equipment and conditions.
- Disconnect the solar panel and trunk head from the electrical system using insulated tools to avoid shock.
- Follow manufacturer guidelines for the installation of replacement components, ensuring correct torque specifications and electrical connections.
- Conduct post-installation testing to validate the electrical integrity and functional performance of the new panel and trunk head.
- Clean the work area and properly dispose of all old components and debris.

**5. Documentation:**
- Maintain a detailed log of all work performed, including start and completion times, staff involved, and any observations made during the project.

**6. Completion Criteria:**
- Successful installation of the new panel and trunk head, passing all functionality tests and ensuring compliance with safety regulations.

Quote.scope_of_work:
**Scope of Work (SOW) for Electrical/Solar Maintenance and Service**

**Project Objective:**
The objective of this project is to relocate higher demanding AC loads to an auxiliary relay to enhance off-grid battery preservation, preventing potential overload issues on the existing backup system.

**Work Description:**
1. **Relocation of Loads:**
   - Identify and assess existing higher demanding loads currently being backed up.
   - Implement the installation of an auxiliary relay contact to divide these loads effectively, ensuring that only necessary loads are powered during outages to preserve battery life.

2. **Installation Steps:**
   - Install 3/4" liquid tight flex conduit along the designated pathways to house new wiring.
   - Use 3/4" liquid tight connectors (4x) to secure the conduit.
   - Run 4x #10 AWG wires (5 feet each) and 2x #18 AWG wires (3 feet each) from the auxiliary relay enclosure to the existing breaker and panel.
   - Install 2x 3/4" liquid tight 1-hole straps to secure the conduit in place.

3. **Testing:**

• Root cause identified as a failed/burnt trunk cable connector affecting the string.
• Customer advised to contact Enphase Customer Support to explore coverage under Enphase Care and potential replacement/repair options.

• System not fully commissioned.
• 9 microinverters remain offline due to wiring failure.

• Re-test circuit integrity and breaker function post-repair.
• Complete provisioning and validation once issue is resolved.

Quote.scope_of_work:
**Scope of Work for Replacement of Damaged Roof Panels and System Testing**

**1. Project Overview**  
This project involves the replacement of two damaged solar roof panels/modules and performing a full system testing to ensure optimal performance and safety.

**2. Tasks to be Performed**  
- **Identify Damage:** Conduct a preliminary inspection of the roof and solar panels to confirm the extent of damage and identify the specific panels/modules that require replacement.
- **Replace Panels/Modules:** Safely remove the damaged panels/modules from the roof. Install two new solar panels/modules that match the existing system specifications.
- **Re-Connect Wiring:** Reconnect all electrical wiring associated with the new panels/modules to the existing solar energy system.
- **Seal and Secure:** Ensure that all new installations are properly sealed to prevent water ingress and that all mechanical fasteners are securely tightened.

**3. System Testing**  
- **Initial Diagnostics:** Perform a comprehensive system diagnostic check before and after the replacement to assess current system performance levels.
- **Operational Testing:** Monitor the output of the refurbished system, including voltage and current from each panel, to confirm functionality.
- **Safety Testing:** Conduct a safety test on the entire electrical system to verify adherence to all relevant electrical codes and standards.

**4. Safety Considerations**  
- **Personal Protective Equipment (PPE):** All personnel must wear appropriate PPE, including hard hats, gloves, and safety glasses, during the project.
- **Electrical Safety:** De-energize the solar system prior to replacing panels/modules and follow Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures to enhance safety during maintenance.
- **Fall Protection:** Utilize safety harnesses and fall protection measures when working on the roof to mitigate fall risks.

**5. Expected Approach/Methodology**  
- **Pre-Project Planning:** Conduct a site survey to assess structural integrity, access points, and potential hazards before starting work.
- **Panel Removal and Installation:** Utilize specialized tools and equipment designed for roof and panel work to ensure fast and secure operations.
- **Post-Installation Testing:** After installation, integrate testing measures using a calibrated solar meter and other diagnostic tools to ensure that all system components are operating at expected performance levels.
- **Documentation:** Provide a report detailing the work performed, including any observations or recommendations for future maintenance, alongside warranty information for the new panels/modules. 

This scope of work aims to ensure the efficient and safe execution of solar panel replacements and comprehensive system testing.

**Scope of Work for Electrical/Solar Maintenance and Service**

**Project Title:** Replacement of Damaged Trunk Cable and Solar Panel DC Cable

**Location:** [25251 Mastery Place, Aldie, VA 20105]

**Description of Work:**

1. **Site Inspection and Assessment:**
   - Conduct a thorough site inspection to assess the extent of the critter damage to the trunk cable and the solar panel DC cable. Document findings with photos and notes for records.

2. **Approval and Coordination:**
   - Obtain written approval from client before commencing work on the replacement of the trunk cable and the damaged solar panel DC cable.
   - Coordinate with local utility providers if necessary to ensure compliance with service interruption protocols and to schedule any required power shutdowns.

3. **Preparation:**
   - Prepare the work area to ensure safe access to the affected solar panels and cables. This includes setting up barriers and signage to alert unauthorized personnel.
   - Gather needed tools and materials including replacement trunk cable, compatible solar panel DC cable, connectors, and safety gear.

4. **Safety Considerations:**
   - Ensure all team members are equipped with personal protective equipment (PPE), including hard hats, safety glasses, gloves, and high-visibility clothing.
   - Verify that all electrical systems have been de-energized and Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures are in place prior to starting work.
   - Implement safety measures to avoid potential hazards from wildlife during repairs, particularly from any nesting critters in the solar array vicinity.

5. **Cable Replacement:**
   - Carefully remove and replace the damaged trunk cable section of the affected string, ensuring that connections are secure and follow manufacturer specifications.
   - Inspect and replace the severely damaged solar panel DC cable, performing continuity tests to confirm proper function post-installation.

6. **Final Inspection and Testing:**
   - Once the replacements are completed, conduct a thorough inspection of all connections and ensure that the repaired system meets operational standards.
   - Reconnect and reactivate the microinverters associated with the replaced cables, monitoring performance to confirm that the system is operational and producing energy as expected.

7. **Documentation and Reporting:**
   - Document all work performed, including before and after photos, materials used, and labor hours.
   - Submit a final report to the client detailing the repairs made, testing results, and recommendations for future maintenance to prevent similar damage.

**End of Scope of Work**

**Scope of Work for Repair and Replacement of Microinverter**

**Project Overview:**
This scope of work outlines the necessary steps to repair the damaged DC leads on the solar panel and replace the issued microinverter to resolve the reporting issue.

**1. Tasks to be Performed:**
   - Conduct a visual inspection of the solar panel and existing wiring to assess the extent of damage.
   - Identify the specific location and extent of the chewed DC leads.
   - Disconnect the affected DC leads from the solar panel and microinverter.
   - Replace the damaged DC leads with new, appropriately rated wiring, ensuring compatibility with the existing system specifications.
   - Connect the new DC leads to the microinverter and ensure secure connections.
   - Test the microinverter to verify proper reporting functionality after the repair.

**2. Safety Considerations:**
   - Ensure all work is conducted in compliance with local electrical codes and safety regulations.
   - Verify that the solar power system is de-energized before beginning any disconnections and repairs.
   - Utilize appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE), including insulated gloves and safety glasses.
   - Implement proper lockout/tagout procedures to prevent the accidental energization of the system during the repair.
   - Maintain a safe working distance from any live electrical components and ensure a clear work zone.

**3. Approach/Methodology:**
   - Schedule the repair during daylight hours to facilitate visibility and ensure safe working conditions.
   - Use insulated tools to perform all electrical work to minimize the risk of electrical shock.
   - Carefully remove the damaged DC leads without causing additional harm to the panel or surrounding components.
   - Employ heat-shrink protection on all connections to enhance durability and prevent environmental damage.
   - Conduct a functional test of the microinverter after reconnection to confirm that it is reporting correctly and is fully operational.
   - Document all findings, repairs made, and test results for future reference and to provide to the client upon project completion.

**Scope of Work for Electrical Maintenance and Service**

**Project Title:** IQ Battery Load Center Installation and System Optimization

**1. Overview:**
The purpose of this scope of work is to ensure proper functioning and integration of the IQ Batteries, AC Combiner, and the IQ Gateway within the existing electrical system. This will involve the addition of a Load Center and the correct configuration of electrical components for optimal relay control.

**2. Work Activities:**

- **Load Center Installation:**
  - Install a Load Center specifically designated for the IQ Batteries to enhance operational efficiency.
  
- **AC Combiner Reconfiguration:**
  - Safely disconnect the AC Combiner from its current configuration.
  - Relocate the wiring currently connected to the 40A breaker located in the Generator slot.
  - Properly connect the relocated wires to the DER lugs in the IQ System Controller to ensure accurate relay functioning.

- **IQ Gateway Relocation:**
  - Disconnect the IQ Gateway from its existing position.
  - Relocate the IQ Gateway Breaker to the Common Bus of the IQ System Controller.

**3. Safety Considerations:**
- All work will be performed in accordance with the National Electrical Code (NEC) and local safety regulations.
- Prior to commencement, conduct a thorough risk assessment to identify potential hazards associated with electrical work, including the risk of electric shock and arc flash.
- Ensure all affected circuit breakers are de-energized and securely locked out/tagged out (LOTO) prior to any wiring modifications.
- Use appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE), including insulated gloves and safety goggles.
- Maintain a clean and organized workspace to minimize trip hazards and contamination.

**4. Methodology:**
- Verify and document existing configurations of the IQ Batteries, AC Combiner, and IQ Gateway before any modifications.
- Utilize appropriate tools and equipment for electrical work, ensuring they are calibrated and in good working condition.
- Follow a systematic approach to rewire and relocate components, maintaining clear communication with all involved personnel.
- Conduct thorough testing of the system post-modification to confirm all components are functioning within the specified parameters before restoring power.
- Provide a comprehensive report detailing all work performed, changes made, and any recommendations for future maintenance or upgrades.

**5. Deliverables:**
- Installed Load Center for IQ Batteries.
- Reconfigured and relocated wiring to DER lugs and IQ Gateway.
- Completion report including schematic diagrams, test results, and safety compliance documentation.

Quote.scope_of_work:
**Scope of Work for Electrical Maintenance and Service**

**Project Title:** IQ Battery Load Center Installation and System Optimization

**1. Overview:**
The purpose of this scope of work is to ensure proper functioning and integration of the IQ Batteries, AC Combiner, and the IQ Gateway within the existing electrical system. This will involve the addition of a Load Center and the correct configuration of electrical components for optimal relay control.

**2. Work Activities:**

- **Load Center Installation:**
  - Install a Load Center specifically designated for the IQ Batteries to enhance operational efficiency.
  
- **AC Combiner Reconfiguration:**
  - Safely disconnect the AC Combiner from its current configuration.
  - Relocate the wiring currently connected to the 40A breaker located in the Generator slot.
  - Properly connect the relocated wires to the DER lugs in the IQ System Controller to ensure accurate relay functioning.

- **IQ Gateway Relocation:**
  - Disconnect the IQ Gateway from its existing position.
  - Relocate the IQ Gateway Breaker to the Common Bus of the IQ System Controller.

**3. Safety Considerations:**
- All work will be performed in accordance with the National Electrical Code (NEC) and local safety regulations.
- Prior to commencement, conduct a thorough risk assessment to identify potential hazards associated with electrical work, including the risk of electric shock and arc flash.
- Ensure all affected circuit breakers are de-energized and securely locked out/tagged out (LOTO) prior to any wiring modifications.
- Use appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE), including insulated gloves and safety goggles.
- Maintain a clean and organized workspace to minimize trip hazards and contamination.

**4. Methodology:**
- Verify and document existing configurations of the IQ Batteries, AC Combiner, and IQ Gateway before any modifications.
- Utilize appropriate tools and equipment for electrical work, ensuring they are calibrated and in good working condition.
- Follow a systematic approach to rewire and relocate components, maintaining clear communication with all involved personnel.
- Conduct thorough testing of the system post-modification to confirm all components are functioning within the specified parameters before restoring power.
- Provide a comprehensive report detailing all work performed, changes made, and any recommendations for future maintenance or upgrades.

**5. Deliverables:**
- Installed Load Center for IQ Batteries.
- Reconfigured and relocated wiring to DER lugs and IQ Gateway.
- Completion report including schematic diagrams, test results, and safety compliance documentation. 

**End of Scope of Work**

**Scope of Work for Replacement of IQSC and Associated Components**

**1. Project Overview:**
This scope addresses the replacement of the entire IQSC due to water intrusion caused by improper installation. The project also includes the removal of the AC unit from the backup loads, which constitutes a design issue.

**2. Tasks to Be Performed:**
- **Removal of Existing IQSC:**
  - Safely disconnect and remove the current IQSC from its mounting position.
  - Carefully inspect all wiring and components for water damage and corrosion, documenting findings for future reference.
  
- **Installation of New IQSC:**
  - Install a new IQSC using a Meyer’s hub connector to ensure a watertight seal at the top penetration.
  - Verify that all electrical connections are secure and compliant with manufacturer specifications and local codes.
  
- **Removal of AC Unit from BLP:**
  - Safely disconnect and remove the backup AC unit from the electrical system.
  - Ensure that the unit is disposed of in accordance with local regulations and guidelines.

**3. Safety Considerations:**
- Prior to commencing work, conduct a site-specific risk assessment to identify potential hazards related to electrical work and water damage.
- Ensure all personnel are equipped with appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE), including gloves, safety glasses, and hard hats.
- Establish de-energization protocols, verifying that all systems are powered down before beginning any work on electrical components.
- Implement measures to prevent water intrusion during installation, especially in adverse weather conditions.

**4. Methodology:**
- Follow standard electrical installation practices and manufacturer guidelines throughout the replacement process.
- Utilize appropriate tools and equipment to execute the removal and installation processes safely and efficiently.
- Document all phases of the work, including before and after photos, wiring diagrams, and any observations related to component integrity.
- Upon completion of all work, conduct a thorough system test to ensure functionality and verify that the new installations meet operational and safety standards. 

**5. Final Inspections:**
- Schedule a final inspection with relevant stakeholders to confirm that all work complies with specifications and addresses the original issues identified in the IQSC and AC unit design. 
- Provide documentation of all inspections and tests performed. 

The completion of this scope will restore the system’s functionality while ensuring compliance with safety regulations and design specifications.

**Images utilized to estimate needs available on Case# 10476871 under SA-73452 from 6/3/25**

Scope of Work for Electrical/Solar Maintenance and Service

Project Summary:
The project involves correcting design and installation issues related to the electrical metering and wiring in the solar power system. This encompasses the relocation of current transformers (CTs) and the upsize of conductors to enhance system performance and safety.

Tasks to be Completed:

1. CCT & Line Side Tap Relocation: 30-60 minutes estimated
Ensure CCTs are installed between the PV Only taps & MSP lugs for optimal functionality and accuracy.
   - Assess and document the current installation of CCTs and the taps of the PV Only system.
   - Relocate PV Only taps 6"-8" further from utility feeder lugs entering MSP 
   - Apply 1/2" heat shrink tubing to re-seal wire insulation at prior tapping location to prevent corrosion etc.
   - Relocate CCTs to compliant position between MSP lugs and PV Only system taps.
   - Run CT Wizard ensuring Backup System CCTs are not measuring export from PV only system taps. 

2. Wiring Inspection and Upgrade: 6 hours estimated
   - Inspect all existing 10-gauge wiring routed into the system controller and from the controller to the backup loads panel.
   - De-energize the system and ensure all safety protocols are in place prior to conducting any inspections or modifications.
   - Replace all 10-gauge wires with appropriately sized 6 or 8-gauge wires in accordance with electrical codes and load calculations.
   - Ensure that all connections are properly secured and that any conduit or raceway is adequately sized for the new wiring.

3. System Testing and Verification: 60 min estimated
   - Reintegrate the system and conduct functional tests to verify that the relocation of the CTs and the upgrade of the wiring meet performance standards and safety regulations.
   - Document all modifications, test results, and compliance with relevant regulations and manufacturer guidelines.

Safety Considerations:
- All work will be performed by qualified electrical personnel with appropriate certifications and training.
- Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures will be strictly enforced during the disconnection of the system.
- Personal protective equipment (PPE) including gloves, goggles, and insulated tools will be used throughout the work.
- Compliance with National Electrical Code (NEC) and local electrical codes will be maintained at all stages.

Expected Approach/Methodology:
- Conduct a pre-work meeting to review project scope, safety protocols, and timeline.
- Utilize project management tools to track progress and ensure completion within the specified timeframe.
- Engage with stakeholders for regular updates and any required approvals during the course of the work.
- Post-completion, a final inspection will be carried out to ensure full compliance with safety standards and operational effectiveness.

**Scope of Work for On-Site Assessment of Electrical/Solar System**

**Project Title:** On-Site Assessment of Solar Battery System  

**Objective:**  
To conduct a thorough assessment of the existing solar system focusing on the battery issues reported due to prior negligent installation practices.  

**Scope of Work:**

1. **Pre-Assessment Preparation:**
   - Review existing installation documentation and previous maintenance logs.
   - Coordinate with the site owner to schedule assessment and ensure access to all equipment.

2. **On-Site Visual Inspection:**
   - Inspect PV, batteries, IQSC, and associated wiring for visible signs of wear, damage, or improper installation.
   - Evaluate the condition of the battery management system (BMS) and other monitoring equipment for operational integrity.

3. **Battery Condition Evaluation:**
   - Conduct a detailed analysis of battery performance including voltage, capacity, and state of charge (SOC) measurements at various points.
   - Utilize appropriate testing equipment (e.g., multimeters, battery analyzers) to assess battery health and potential issues such as sulfation or cell imbalance.

4. **Electrical Connections Verification:**
   - Examine all electrical connections for corrosion, loose terminals, and compliance with local electrical codes.
   - Assess the configuration and functionality of wiring and fuses within the system, ensuring they meet manufacturer specifications.

5. **Safety Considerations:**
   - Adhere to all local and national electrical safety standards, including PPE (Personal Protective Equipment) requirements such as gloves, goggles, and insulated tools.
   - Implement lock-out/tag-out (LOTO) procedures for working on electrical systems to ensure no accidental energization.
   - Ensure proper ventilation and emergency protocols are in place when working near batteries to mitigate risks associated with potentially hazardous gases.

6. **Analysis and Reporting:**
   - Document findings in a comprehensive report detailing the assessment results, indicating any improper installations or required corrections.
   - Provide recommendations for maintenance, repair, or replacement of components as necessary to enhance system reliability and performance.

7. **Follow-Up:**
   - Discuss findings with the site owner and provide guidance on corrective actions.
   - Suggest a schedule for regular maintenance checks to prevent future issues and ensure system longevity.

**Expected Approach/Methodology:**
   - The assessment will be performed systematically, following industry best practices using calibrated testing tools and methodologies.  
   - Collaboration with stakeholders throughout the process to ensure clarity and alignment on findings and recommendations.  
   - Priority on safety and compliance, with a focus on restoring system functionality and optimizing the performance of the solar energy setup.  

**Completion Criteria:**
   - Comprehensive report on system status and recommendations submitted to the site owner.
   - Follow-up meeting scheduled to review findings and proposed actions.

**Scope of Work for Replacement of IQSC and Associated Components**

**1. Project Overview:**
This scope addresses the replacement of the entire IQSC due to water intrusion caused by improper installation. The project also includes the removal of the AC unit from the backup loads, which constitutes a design issue.

**2. Tasks to Be Performed:**
- **Removal of Existing IQSC:**
  - Safely disconnect and remove the current IQSC from its mounting position.
  - Carefully inspect all wiring and components for water damage and corrosion, documenting findings for future reference.
  
- **Installation of New IQSC:**
  - Install a new IQSC using a Meyer’s hub connector to ensure a watertight seal at the top penetration.
  - Verify that all electrical connections are secure and compliant with manufacturer specifications and local codes.
  
- **Removal of AC Unit from BLP:**
  - Safely disconnect and remove the backup AC unit from the electrical system.
  - Ensure that the unit is disposed of in accordance with local regulations and guidelines.

**3. Safety Considerations:**
- Prior to commencing work, conduct a site-specific risk assessment to identify potential hazards related to electrical work and water damage.
- Ensure all personnel are equipped with appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE), including gloves, safety glasses, and hard hats.
- Establish de-energization protocols, verifying that all systems are powered down before beginning any work on electrical components.
- Implement measures to prevent water intrusion during installation, especially in adverse weather conditions.

**4. Methodology:**
- Follow standard electrical installation practices and manufacturer guidelines throughout the replacement process.
- Utilize appropriate tools and equipment to execute the removal and installation processes safely and efficiently.
- Document all phases of the work, including before and after photos, wiring diagrams, and any observations related to component integrity.
- Upon completion of all work, conduct a thorough system test to ensure functionality and verify that the new installations meet operational and safety standards. 

**5. Final Inspections:**
- Schedule a final inspection with relevant stakeholders to confirm that all work complies with specifications and addresses the original issues identified in the IQSC and AC unit design. 
- Provide documentation of all inspections and tests performed. 

The completion of this scope will restore the system’s functionality while ensuring compliance with safety regulations and design specifications.

Quote.scope_of_work:
**Scope of Work (SOW) for Electrical/Solar Maintenance and Service**

**Project Objective:**
The objective of this project is to relocate higher demanding AC loads to an auxiliary relay to enhance off-grid battery preservation, preventing potential overload issues on the existing backup system.

**Work Description:**
1. **Relocation of Loads:**
   - Identify and assess existing higher demanding loads currently being backed up.
   - Implement the installation of an auxiliary relay contact to divide these loads effectively, ensuring that only necessary loads are powered during outages to preserve battery life.

2. **Installation Steps:**
   - Install 3/4" liquid tight flex conduit along the designated pathways to house new wiring.
   - Use 3/4" liquid tight connectors (4x) to secure the conduit.
   - Run 4x #10 AWG wires (5 feet each) and 2x #18 AWG wires (3 feet each) from the auxiliary relay enclosure to the existing breaker and panel.
   - Install 2x 3/4" liquid tight 1-hole straps to secure the conduit in place.

3. **Testing:**
   - Conduct thorough testing of the auxiliary relay and its integration with the existing system to ensure proper functionality during outages. Confirm that loads are appropriately managed and that the battery preservation measures are effective.

**Safety Considerations:**
- Utilize appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE), including gloves, safety glasses, and insulated tools while performing electrical work.
- Ensure all power sources are de-energized prior to beginning installation to prevent electrical shock or injury.
- Follow all local electrical codes and safety guidelines relevant to off-grid systems during installation and testing procedures.

**Expected Approach/Methodology:**
- Begin with a comprehensive site assessment to identify load demands and existing wiring configurations.
- Proceed with the installation of conduit and wiring while adhering to safety protocols and manufacturer's instructions for electrical components.
- Utilize best practices for installation and ensure that all connections and terminations are secure.
- Complete testing of the system post-installation to validate the effectiveness of the auxiliary relay in managing loads during outages.

**Documentation:**
- Capture and upload relevant pictures and video of the installation process and completed setup to the project case within SFDC.
- Provide receipts for all materials purchased as part of the project for record-keeping and reimbursement clarity.

**Scope of Work for Electrical/Solar Maintenance Service**

**Project Title:** Critter Damage Inspection and Repair

**Location:** [8006 Crichton Lane, Durham, NC 27713]

**Objective:**
Conduct an inspection and repair of two solar arrays affected by critter damage, and provide options for mitigation through the installation of critter guards.

**Tasks to be Performed:**

1. **Site Inspection:**
   - Conduct a thorough visual inspection of the two affected solar arrays to assess the extent of critter damage.
   - Document findings and take photographic evidence for records.

2. **Repair Work:**
   - Replace damaged connectors with one drop of IQ micro connector cable.
   - Install two new terminator caps on the affected areas to ensure complete sealing and prevent further damage.

3. **Installation of Critter Guard (if requested by the customer):**
   - Discuss and confirm the installation of critter guard netting around all arrays.
   - Calculate approximately 200 feet of netting required for full coverage.
   - Install the critter guard netting, ensuring proper tension and secure attachment to prevent critter access.

**Safety Considerations:**
- All technicians will adhere to OSHA safety regulations and industry best practices to ensure a safe work environment.
- Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) such as gloves, helmets, and safety glasses must be worn at all times.
- All electrical systems will be evaluated and de-energized prior to starting work to minimize risk of electrical shock.
- Technicians will be briefed on site safety protocols, including identifying and mitigating any hazards present on the site.

**Expected Approach/Methodology:**
- Two qualified technicians will be deployed to the site for an estimated four hours to complete the inspection and repairs.
- Technicians will use appropriate tools and equipment to safely access solar array installations and perform necessary repairs.
- After repairs are made, the site will be cleaned of any debris generated during the work to ensure the area is returned to its original condition.
- A follow-up report detailing the completed work and any additional recommendations will be provided to the customer post-service.

**Conclusion:**
This Scope of Work outlines the necessary actions to inspect and repair critter damage to the solar arrays and provides options for preventative measures against future incidents. The work will be conducted efficiently and safely, prioritizing the satisfaction and safety of our customer.

Quote.scope_of_work:
**Images utilized to estimate needs available on Case# 10476871 under SA-73452 from 6/3/25**

Scope of Work for Electrical/Solar Maintenance and Service

Project Summary:
The project involves correcting design and installation issues related to the electrical metering and wiring in the solar power system. This encompasses the relocation of current transformers (CTs) and the upsize of conductors to enhance system performance and safety.

Tasks to be Completed:

1. CCT & Line Side Tap Relocation: 30-60 minutes estimated
Ensure CCTs are installed between the PV Only taps & MSP lugs for optimal functionality and accuracy.
   - Assess and document the current installation of CCTs and the taps of the PV Only system.
   - Relocate PV Only taps 6"-8" further from utility feeder lugs entering MSP 
   - Apply 1/2" heat shrink tubing to re-seal wire insulation at prior tapping location to prevent corrosion etc.
   - Relocate CCTs to compliant position between MSP lugs and PV Only system taps.
   - Run CT Wizard ensuring Backup System CCTs are not measuring export from PV only system taps. 

2. Wiring Inspection and Upgrade: 6 hours estimated
   - Inspect all existing 10-gauge wiring routed into the system controller and from the controller to the backup loads panel.
   - De-energize the system and ensure all safety protocols are in place prior to conducting any inspections or modifications.
   - Replace all 10-gauge wires with appropriately sized 6 or 8-gauge wires in accordance with electrical codes and load calculations.
   - Ensure that all connections are properly secured and that any conduit or raceway is adequately sized for the new wiring.

3. System Testing and Verification: 60 min estimated
   - Reintegrate the system and conduct functional tests to verify that the relocation of the CTs and the upgrade of the wiring meet performance standards and safety regulations.
   - Document all modifications, test results, and compliance with relevant regulations and manufacturer guidelines.

Safety Considerations:
- All work will be performed by qualified electrical personnel with appropriate certifications and training.
- Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures will be strictly enforced during the disconnection of the system.
- Personal protective equipment (PPE) including gloves, goggles, and insulated tools will be used throughout the work.
- Compliance with National Electrical Code (NEC) and local electrical codes will be maintained at all stages.

Expected Approach/Methodology:
- Conduct a pre-work meeting to review project scope, safety protocols, and timeline.
- Utilize project management tools to track progress and ensure completion within the specified timeframe.
- Engage with stakeholders for regular updates and any required approvals during the course of the work.
- Post-completion, a final inspection will be carried out to ensure full compliance with safety standards and operational effectiveness.

Quote.scope_of_work:
**Scope of Work for Electrical/Solar Maintenance and Service**

**Project Title:** Replacement of Damaged Trunk Cable and Solar Panel DC Cable

**Location:** [25251 Mastery Place, Aldie, VA 20105]

**Description of Work:**

1. **Site Inspection and Assessment:**
   - Conduct a thorough site inspection to assess the extent of the critter damage to the trunk cable and the solar panel DC cable. Document findings with photos and notes for records.

2. **Approval and Coordination:**
   - Obtain written approval from client before commencing work on the replacement of the trunk cable and the damaged solar panel DC cable.
   - Coordinate with local utility providers if necessary to ensure compliance with service interruption protocols and to schedule any required power shutdowns.

3. **Preparation:**
   - Prepare the work area to ensure safe access to the affected solar panels and cables. This includes setting up barriers and signage to alert unauthorized personnel.
   - Gather needed tools and materials including replacement trunk cable, compatible solar panel DC cable, connectors, and safety gear.

4. **Safety Considerations:**
   - Ensure all team members are equipped with personal protective equipment (PPE), including hard hats, safety glasses, gloves, and high-visibility clothing.
   - Verify that all electrical systems have been de-energized and Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures are in place prior to starting work.
   - Implement safety measures to avoid potential hazards from wildlife during repairs, particularly from any nesting critters in the solar array vicinity.

5. **Cable Replacement:**
   - Carefully remove and replace the damaged trunk cable section of the affected string, ensuring that connections are secure and follow manufacturer specifications.
   - Inspect and replace the severely damaged solar panel DC cable, performing continuity tests to confirm proper function post-installation.

6. **Final Inspection and Testing:**
   - Once the replacements are completed, conduct a thorough inspection of all connections and ensure that the repaired system meets operational standards.
   - Reconnect and reactivate the microinverters associated with the replaced cables, monitoring performance to confirm that the system is operational and producing energy as expected.

7. **Documentation and Reporting:**
   - Document all work performed, including before and after photos, materials used, and labor hours.
   - Submit a final report to the client detailing the repairs made, testing results, and recommendations for future maintenance to prevent similar damage.

**End of Scope of Work**

**Scope of Work for Electrical/Solar Maintenance and Service**

**Project Title:** Replacement of Damaged Trunk Cable and Solar Panel DC Cable

**Location:** [25251 Mastery Place, Aldie, VA 20105]

**Description of Work:**

1. **Site Inspection and Assessment:**
   - Conduct a thorough site inspection to assess the extent of the critter damage to the trunk cable and the solar panel DC cable. Document findings with photos and notes for records.

2. **Approval and Coordination:**
   - Obtain written approval from client before commencing work on the replacement of the trunk cable and the damaged solar panel DC cable.
   - Coordinate with local utility providers if necessary to ensure compliance with service interruption protocols and to schedule any required power shutdowns.

3. **Preparation:**
   - Prepare the work area to ensure safe access to the affected solar panels and cables. This includes setting up barriers and signage to alert unauthorized personnel.
   - Gather needed tools and materials including replacement trunk cable, compatible solar panel DC cable, connectors, and safety gear.

4. **Safety Considerations:**
   - Ensure all team members are equipped with personal protective equipment (PPE), including hard hats, safety glasses, gloves, and high-visibility clothing.
   - Verify that all electrical systems have been de-energized and Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures are in place prior to starting work.
   - Implement safety measures to avoid potential hazards from wildlife during repairs, particularly from any nesting critters in the solar array vicinity.

5. **Cable Replacement:**
   - Carefully remove and replace the damaged trunk cable section of the affected string, ensuring that connections are secure and follow manufacturer specifications.
   - Inspect and replace the severely damaged solar panel DC cable, performing continuity tests to confirm proper function post-installation.

6. **Final Inspection and Testing:**
   - Once the replacements are completed, conduct a thorough inspection of all connections and ensure that the repaired system meets operational standards.
   - Reconnect and reactivate the microinverters associated with the replaced cables, monitoring performance to confirm that the system is operational and producing energy as expected.

7. **Documentation and Reporting:**
   - Document all work performed, including before and after photos, materials used, and labor hours.
   - Submit a final report to the client detailing the repairs made, testing results, and recommendations for future maintenance to prevent similar damage.

**End of Scope of Work**

Quote.scope_of_work:
**Scope of Work for Electrical/Solar Maintenance Service**

**Project Title:** Critter Damage Inspection and Repair

**Location:** [8006 Crichton Lane, Durham, NC 27713]

**Objective:**
Conduct an inspection and repair of two solar arrays affected by critter damage, and provide options for mitigation through the installation of critter guards.

**Tasks to be Performed:**

1. **Site Inspection:**
   - Conduct a thorough visual inspection of the two affected solar arrays to assess the extent of critter damage.
   - Document findings and take photographic evidence for records.

2. **Repair Work:**
   - Replace damaged connectors with one drop of IQ micro connector cable.
   - Install two new terminator caps on the affected areas to ensure complete sealing and prevent further damage.

3. **Installation of Critter Guard (if requested by the customer):**
   - Discuss and confirm the installation of critter guard netting around all arrays.
   - Calculate approximately 200 feet of netting required for full coverage.
   - Install the critter guard netting, ensuring proper tension and secure attachment to prevent critter access.

**Safety Considerations:**
- All technicians will adhere to OSHA safety regulations and industry best practices to ensure a safe work environment.
- Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) such as gloves, helmets, and safety glasses must be worn at all times.
- All electrical systems will be evaluated and de-energized prior to starting work to minimize risk of electrical shock.
- Technicians will be briefed on site safety protocols, including identifying and mitigating any hazards present on the site.

**Expected Approach/Methodology:**
- Two qualified technicians will be deployed to the site for an estimated four hours to complete the inspection and repairs.
- Technicians will use appropriate tools and equipment to safely access solar array installations and perform necessary repairs.
- After repairs are made, the site will be cleaned of any debris generated during the work to ensure the area is returned to its original condition.
- A follow-up report detailing the completed work and any additional recommendations will be provided to the customer post-service.

**Conclusion:**
This Scope of Work outlines the necessary actions to inspect and repair critter damage to the solar arrays and provides options for preventative measures against future incidents. The work will be conducted efficiently and safely, prioritizing the satisfaction and safety of our customer.

Quote.scope_of_work:
**Images utilized to estimate needs available on Case# 10476871 under SA-73452 from 6/3/25**

Scope of Work for Electrical/Solar Maintenance and Service

Project Summary:
The project involves correcting design and installation issues related to the electrical metering and wiring in the solar power system. This encompasses the relocation of current transformers (CTs) and the upsize of conductors to enhance system performance and safety.

Tasks to be Completed:

1. CCT & Line Side Tap Relocation: 30-60 minutes estimated
Ensure CCTs are installed between the PV Only taps & MSP lugs for optimal functionality and accuracy.
   - Assess and document the current installation of CCTs and the taps of the PV Only system.
   - Relocate PV Only taps 6"-8" further from utility feeder lugs entering MSP 
   - Apply 1/2" heat shrink tubing to re-seal wire insulation at prior tapping location to prevent corrosion etc.
   - Relocate CCTs to compliant position between MSP lugs and PV Only system taps.
   - Run CT Wizard ensuring Backup System CCTs are not measuring export from PV only system taps. 

2. Wiring Inspection and Upgrade: 6 hours estimated
   - Inspect all existing 10-gauge wiring routed into the system controller and from the controller to the backup loads panel.
   - De-energize the system and ensure all safety protocols are in place prior to conducting any inspections or modifications.
   - Replace all 10-gauge wires with appropriately sized 6 or 8-gauge wires in accordance with electrical codes and load calculations.
   - Ensure that all connections are properly secured and that any conduit or raceway is adequately sized for the new wiring.

3. System Testing and Verification: 60 min estimated
   - Reintegrate the system and conduct functional tests to verify that the relocation of the CTs and the upgrade of the wiring meet performance standards and safety regulations.
   - Document all modifications, test results, and compliance with relevant regulations and manufacturer guidelines.

Safety Considerations:
- All work will be performed by qualified electrical personnel with appropriate certifications and training.
- Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures will be strictly enforced during the disconnection of the system.
- Personal protective equipment (PPE) including gloves, goggles, and insulated tools will be used throughout the work.
- Compliance with National Electrical Code (NEC) and local electrical codes will be maintained at all stages.

Expected Approach/Methodology:
- Conduct a pre-work meeting to review project scope, safety protocols, and timeline.
- Utilize project management tools to track progress and ensure completion within the specified timeframe.
- Engage with stakeholders for regular updates and any required approvals during the course of the work.
- Post-completion, a final inspection will be carried out to ensure full compliance with safety standards and operational effectiveness.

   - Document all work performed, including before and after photos, materials used, and labor hours.

• Replace damaged trunk cable section/connector.
• Re-test circuit integrity and breaker function post-repair.
• Complete provisioning and validation once issue is resolved.

• Accessed roof to retrieve serial numbers for the remaining 9 microinverters.
• Successfully collected all required S/Ns and scanned into ITK.
• Began provisioning and system validation process.
Issue Identified:
• The 9 microinverters failed to communicate during commissioning.
• No voltage detected from the affected units.
• Breaker associated with the circuit was found tripped and repeatedly tripping upon reset.
Troubleshooting Actions:
• Returned to roof for further inspection.
• Lifted module and identified a damaged connector within the trunk cable.
• Upon inspection, connector was broken and showed signs of burn/failure (fried).
• Photos of the damage were captured for documentation.
Resolution / Next Steps:
• Root cause identified as a failed/burnt trunk cable connector affecting the string.
• Customer advised to contact Enphase Customer Support to explore coverage under Enphase Care and potential replacement/repair options.
• Repair cannot proceed until approval/replacement materials are obtained.
System Status:
• System not fully commissioned.
• 9 microinverters remain offline due to wiring failure.
Recommendations:
• Replace damaged trunk cable section/connector.
• Re-test circuit integrity and breaker function post-repair.
• Complete provisioning and validation once issue is resolved.

Quote.scope_of_work:
**Scope of Work for Electrical/Solar Maintenance and Service**

**Project Title:** Microinverter Replacement and System Enhancement

**Objective:** To replace failed microinverters and enhance system protections and metering capabilities.

**Tasks:**

1. **Return Material Authorization (RMA) Process:**
   - Initiate and complete the RMA process for the replacement of 44 failed microinverters.
   - Coordinate with the supplier for the procurement and shipment of new microinverters.

2. **Installation of Q-Relay:** << Working on if needed 
   - Assess the current system to determine the necessity of installing a Q-relay.
   - If applicable, install a Q-relay to protect the new microinverters against potential Overvoltage Events (OVE) damage.
   - Ensure protection for 4 strings of microinverters as specified.

3. **Communication Cable Installation:**
   - Return to the site equipped with approximately 40 ft of sunlight-resistant 18-4 communications cable.
   - Replace or install the communications cable as needed to ensure reliable communication between system components.

4. **Relocation of Consumption CTs:**
   - Safely relocate the consumption current transformers (CTs) to the line-side feeders of the System Controller.
   - Ensure accurate metering by verifying the correct placement and connection of the CTs.

**Safety Considerations:**
- Adhere to all applicable electrical codes and safety standards during the handling and installation of electrical components.
- Implement lockout/tagout (LOTO) procedures before commencing work on the electrical system to ensure a safe working environment.
- Use personal protective equipment (PPE) such as gloves, safety glasses, and hard hats where necessary.
- Conduct a thorough risk assessment prior to starting the project, identifying any potential hazards associated with confined space or overhead work.

**Expected Approach/Methodology:**
- Prepare a detailed project plan that outlines timelines and delivery expectations for materials.
- Work under the supervision of a qualified electrical technician to ensure compliance with regulatory standards.
- Use systematic troubleshooting protocols to check all connections after installation and ensure functionality of new components.
- Test the entire system post-installation to confirm the operational integrity of the microinverters, Q-relay, communications, and CTs.

**Deliverables:**
- Replacement of 44 microinverters and completion of the RMA process.
- Installed Q-relay with operational verification.
- Installed 18-4 communications cable with testing for functionality.
- Relocated and verified consumption CT placement for accurate metering.

**Completion Timeline:** To be determined after material arrival and scheduling of site visit.

Quote.scope_of_work:
PROJECT: Enphase Gateway Communication Stabilization
Customer Issue: Persistent Zigbee communication drops between Gateway and R1/R2 Battery/Controller stack due to multiple wall obstructions and 35ft distance.
OPTION 1: Gateway Relocation (Recommended Permanent Fix)
Scope of Work: Relocate Gateway to the garage for direct line-of-sight with the System Controller 2 and 4x IQ Batteries.
• Labor: 2 Technicians / Full Day (16 Man-Hours). Includes removal of 3 modules for roof access, conduit bending, wire pull, and system re-commissioning.
• Infrastructure: * ~45ft of 3/4" conduit across the roof.
• Waterproof roof penetration with junction box (Soladeck or equivalent) and 10ft interior garage drop.
• 75ft CT extension run (Shielded Twisted Pair) from MSP to new Gateway location for accurate consumption monitoring.
• Wiring: * 4 x #10 AWG (Hots) and 1 x #8 AWG (Ground) for the roof run.
• 1 x #10 AWG (Neutral) local pull from System Controller to Gateway.
Bill of Materials (BOM):
• 60' 3/4" Conduit & Fittings
• 200' #10 THWN-2 (Hots)
• 55' #8 THWN-2 (Ground)
• 5' #10 THWN-2 (Neutral)
• 100' 18/2 Shielded Twisted Pair (CT Extensions)
• 1x Roof J-Box & Flashing Kit
• Roof Sealant/Caulk
OPTION 2: Zigbee Range Extender (Alternative)
Scope of Work: Install an Enphase Wireless Range Extender (COMMS-24-EXT-01) at a midpoint 120V outlet between the MSP and the Garage.
• Labor: 1 Technician / 1-2 Hours (Installation and ITK Signal Validation).
• Pros: Lower cost; no roof penetration.
• Cons: Does not eliminate physical distance; may still experience signal lag depending on wall density (stucco/wire mesh).
Technician Notes for Pricing:
• Option 1 is labor-intensive due to the requirement of pulling 3 solar panels to complete the conduit run and the 75ft CT extension.
• Relocation is the only 100% guaranteed fix for R1/R2 communication stability in this home layout.

**Scope of Work for Electrical/Solar Maintenance and Service**

**Project Title:** Functional Validation and Maintenance of Solar Power System

**Objective:** To address operational faults detected in the solar power system, specifically the replacement of fuses in the disconnect and troubleshooting of microinverters not reporting.

**Tasks to Be Performed:**

1. **Site Assessment:**
   - Conduct a thorough visual inspection of the entire solar power system including photovoltaic panels, inverters, and electrical disconnects.
   - Review and document live data logs to identify and confirm faults within the system.

2. **Fuse Replacement:**
   - De-energize the disconnect and lockout/tagout (LOTO) the electrical system to ensure safety during maintenance.
   - Remove and replace all faulty fuses within the disconnect as indicated by testing results.
   - Ensure new fuses are compatible with the system specifications and adhere to the manufacturer's recommendations.

3. **Microinverter Troubleshooting:**
   - Inspect all microinverters for signs of physical damage or wear.
   - Verify all connections are secure and all cables are intact, particularly those linked to communication and power.
   - Update firmware if necessary and perform a reset on all affected microinverters to restore functionality.
   - Test each microinverter to confirm they are reporting correctly and integrate with the overall system monitoring platform.

4. **System Testing and Validation:**
   - Re-energize the system following the successful completion of fuse replacement and microinverter repairs.
   - Conduct further live data checks to ensure all components are functioning within normal operational parameters.

**Scope of Work**

**Project Title:** Replacement of 30A AC Disconnect with 60A Disconnect and Fuse Replacement

**Overview:**
This scope of work details the tasks necessary for the installation of a new 60A AC disconnect and the removal of incompatible 60A fuses from the existing 30A AC disconnect at the specified site. The goal is to ensure the electrical system operates safely and efficiently within the required parameters.

**Tasks to be Completed:**

1. **Site Assessment:**
   - Conduct a thorough site evaluation to confirm existing wiring configurations, grounding systems, and direct access to the current 30A AC disconnect.
   - Identify all equipment impacted by the disconnect replacement and any potential hazards in the work area.

2. **Preparation:**
   - Notify relevant stakeholders of the planned service outage and secure necessary approvals for the work to proceed.
   - Gather all required materials including a new 60A AC disconnect, appropriate feeder wires, circuit breakers, and safety gear.

3. **Installation of 60A AC Disconnect:**
   - De-energize the current 30A AC disconnect and verify that all circuits are safe to work on via multimeter testing.
   - Remove the existing 30A AC disconnect from its mounting location, ensuring all associated connections are safely disconnected.
   - Install the new 60A AC disconnect in the designated location, ensuring proper alignment and secure mounting.
   - Connect appropriate size feeder wires compliant with electrical codes and ensure compatibility with the new disconnect.

4. **Removal of Current Fuses:**
   - Safely remove the 60A fuses from the existing 30A disconnect, ensuring there is no risk of electrical shock or equipment damage during the process.
   - Dispose of the removed fuses according to local regulations for hazardous waste.

5. **Inspection and Testing:**
   - Once the installation is complete, engage in a comprehensive inspection of all connections to ascertain compliance with applicable safety standards.
   - Energize the new 60A AC disconnect and conduct testing to verify proper operation and load handling.
   - Document all changes made and record any findings during the installation process.

**Safety Considerations:**
- Ensure all personnel involved in the task are equipped with personal protective equipment (PPE), including gloves, safety glasses, and insulated tools.
- Follow lockout/tagout (LOTO) procedures to guarantee that the system remains in a de-energized state during installation.
- Maintain clear communication with the project team to monitor safety conditions and operational hazards throughout the execution of the work.

**Expected Approach/Methodology:**
The approach will prioritize adherence to the National Electrical Code (NEC) and any relevant local electrical codes, ensuring that all installations are compliant and safe. The work will be conducted systematically, with an emphasis on diagnostics, safe immediate disconnect features, and traceability of all components used. Post-installation, a follow-up inspection will be scheduled to confirm the integrity and performance of the system. Documentation will be kept for future reference and potential future needs.

**Scope of Work**

**Project Title:** Replacement of 30A AC Disconnect with 60A Disconnect and Fuse Replacement

**Overview:**
This scope of work details the tasks necessary for the installation of a new 60A AC disconnect and the removal of incompatible 60A fuses from the existing 30A AC disconnect at the specified site. The goal is to ensure the electrical system operates safely and efficiently within the required parameters.

**Tasks to be Completed:**

1. **Site Assessment:**
   - Conduct a thorough site evaluation to confirm existing wiring configurations, grounding systems, and direct access to the current 30A AC disconnect.
   - Identify all equipment impacted by the disconnect replacement and any potential hazards in the work area.

2. **Preparation:**
   - Notify relevant stakeholders of the planned service outage and secure necessary approvals for the work to proceed.
   - Gather all required materials including a new 60A AC disconnect, appropriate feeder wires, circuit breakers, and safety gear.

3. **Installation of 60A AC Disconnect:**
   - De-energize the current 30A AC disconnect and verify that all circuits are safe to work on via multimeter testing.
   - Remove the existing 30A AC disconnect from its mounting location, ensuring all associated connections are safely disconnected.
   - Install the new 60A AC disconnect in the designated location, ensuring proper alignment and secure mounting.
   - Connect appropriate size feeder wires compliant with electrical codes and ensure compatibility with the new disconnect.

4. **Removal of Current Fuses:**
   - Safely remove the 60A fuses from the existing 30A disconnect, ensuring there is no risk of electrical shock or equipment damage during the process.
   - Dispose of the removed fuses according to local regulations for hazardous waste.

5. **Inspection and Testing:**
   - Once the installation is complete, engage in a comprehensive inspection of all connections to ascertain compliance with applicable safety standards.
   - Energize the new 60A AC disconnect and conduct testing to verify proper operation and load handling.
   - Document all changes made and record any findings during the installation process.

**Safety Considerations:**
- Ensure all personnel involved in the task are equipped with personal protective equipment (PPE), including gloves, safety glasses, and insulated tools.
- Follow lockout/tagout (LOTO) procedures to guarantee that the system remains in a de-energized state during installation.
- Maintain clear communication with the project team to monitor safety conditions and operational hazards throughout the execution of the work.

**Expected Approach/Methodology:**
The approach will prioritize adherence to the National Electrical Code (NEC) and any relevant local electrical codes, ensuring that all installations are compliant and safe. The work will be conducted systematically, with an emphasis on diagnostics, safe immediate disconnect features, and traceability of all components used. Post-installation, a follow-up inspection will be scheduled to confirm the integrity and performance of the system. Documentation will be kept for future reference and potential future needs.

Quote.notes:
**Scope of Work**

**Project Title:** Replacement of 30A AC Disconnect with 60A Disconnect and Fuse Replacement

**Overview:**
This scope of work details the tasks necessary for the installation of a new 60A AC disconnect and the removal of incompatible 60A fuses from the existing 30A AC disconnect at the specified site. The goal is to ensure the electrical system operates safely and efficiently within the required parameters.

**Tasks to be Completed:**

1. **Site Assessment:**
   - Conduct a thorough site evaluation to confirm existing wiring configurations, grounding systems, and direct access to the current 30A AC disconnect.
   - Identify all equipment impacted by the disconnect replacement and any potential hazards in the work area.

2. **Preparation:**
   - Notify relevant stakeholders of the planned service outage and secure necessary approvals for the work to proceed.
   - Gather all required materials including a new 60A AC disconnect, appropriate feeder wires, circuit breakers, and safety gear.

3. **Installation of 60A AC Disconnect:**
   - De-energize the current 30A AC disconnect and verify that all circuits are safe to work on via multimeter testing.
   - Remove the existing 30A AC disconnect from its mounting location, ensuring all associated connections are safely disconnected.
   - Install the new 60A AC disconnect in the designated location, ensuring proper alignment and secure mounting.
   - Connect appropriate size feeder wires compliant with electrical codes and ensure compatibility with the new disconnect.

4. **Removal of Current Fuses:**
   - Safely remove the 60A fuses from the existing 30A disconnect, ensuring there is no risk of electrical shock or equipment damage during the process.
   - Dispose of the removed fuses according to local regulations for hazardous waste.

5. **Inspection and Testing:**
   - Once the installation is complete, engage in a comprehensive inspection of all connections to ascertain compliance with applicable safety standards.
   - Energize the new 60A AC disconnect and conduct testing to verify proper operation and load handling.
   - Document all changes made and record any findings during the installation process.

**Safety Considerations:**
- Ensure all personnel involved in the task are equipped with personal protective equipment (PPE), including gloves, safety glasses, and insulated tools.
- Follow lockout/tagout (LOTO) procedures to guarantee that the system remains in a de-energized state during installation.
- Maintain clear communication with the project team to monitor safety conditions and operational hazards throughout the execution of the work.

**Expected Approach/Methodology:**
The approach will prioritize adherence to the National Electrical Code (NEC) and any relevant local electrical codes, ensuring that all installations are compliant and safe. The work will be conducted systematically, with an emphasis on diagnostics, safe immediate disconnect features, and traceability of all components used. Post-installation, a follow-up inspection will be scheduled to confirm the integrity and performance of the system. Documentation will be kept for future reference and potential future needs.

Quote.notes:
**Scope of Work**

**Project Title:** Replacement of 30A AC Disconnect with 60A Disconnect and Fuse Replacement

**Overview:**
This scope of work details the tasks necessary for the installation of a new 60A AC disconnect and the removal of incompatible 60A fuses from the existing 30A AC disconnect at the specified site. The goal is to ensure the electrical system operates safely and efficiently within the required parameters.

**Tasks to be Completed:**

1. **Site Assessment:**
   - Conduct a thorough site evaluation to confirm existing wiring configurations, grounding systems, and direct access to the current 30A AC disconnect.
   - Identify all equipment impacted by the disconnect replacement and any potential hazards in the work area.

2. **Preparation:**
   - Notify relevant stakeholders of the planned service outage and secure necessary approvals for the work to proceed.
   - Gather all required materials including a new 60A AC disconnect, appropriate feeder wires, circuit breakers, and safety gear.

3. **Installation of 60A AC Disconnect:**
   - De-energize the current 30A AC disconnect and verify that all circuits are safe to work on via multimeter testing.
   - Remove the existing 30A AC disconnect from its mounting location, ensuring all associated connections are safely disconnected.
   - Install the new 60A AC disconnect in the designated location, ensuring proper alignment and secure mounting.
   - Connect appropriate size feeder wires compliant with electrical codes and ensure compatibility with the new disconnect.

4. **Removal of Current Fuses:**
   - Safely remove the 60A fuses from the existing 30A disconnect, ensuring there is no risk of electrical shock or equipment damage during the process.
   - Dispose of the removed fuses according to local regulations for hazardous waste.

5. **Inspection and Testing:**
   - Once the installation is complete, engage in a comprehensive inspection of all connections to ascertain compliance with applicable safety standards.
   - Energize the new 60A AC disconnect and conduct testing to verify proper operation and load handling.
   - Document all changes made and record any findings during the installation process.

**Safety Considerations:**
- Ensure all personnel involved in the task are equipped with personal protective equipment (PPE), including gloves, safety glasses, and insulated tools.
- Follow lockout/tagout (LOTO) procedures to guarantee that the system remains in a de-energized state during installation.
- Maintain clear communication with the project team to monitor safety conditions and operational hazards throughout the execution of the work.

**Expected Approach/Methodology:**
The approach will prioritize adherence to the National Electrical Code (NEC) and any relevant local electrical codes, ensuring that all installations are compliant and safe. The work will be conducted systematically, with an emphasis on diagnostics, safe immediate disconnect features, and traceability of all components used. Post-installation, a follow-up inspection will be scheduled to confirm the integrity and performance of the system. Documentation will be kept for future reference and potential future needs.

Scope of Work
Furnish and install a new junction box and perform a complete replacement of the existing PV system wiring. Scope includes removal of existing wiring (if required), installation of new conductors, proper termination of all circuits, and verification of safe, NEC‑compliant connections.
---
System Details
Total Circuits: 3
Inverters: 38 × Enphase IQ8PLUS‑72‑2‑US
---
Wiring Requirements
AC Wiring – IQ Combiner to Junction Box
Conductor Sizes:
#10 AWG — Black, Red
#8 AWG — Equipment Ground
Approximate Distance: 25 feet
Scope: Route new AC conductors from the IQ Combiner to the newly installed junction box.
---
AC Wiring – PV Modules to Junction Box
Configuration:
(2) Trunk cables
Male and female Enphase Q‑Comm connectors
Purpose: Splice trunk cables inside the new junction box
Conductor Size: #10 AWG
Approximate Distance: 2 feet
Scope: Transition from solar panel trunk cables into the junction box and complete splicing.
---
Materials Required
Junction Box: 6” × 7” × 5” deep
Grounding Hardware:
(1) ¾” ground bushing installed inside the junction box
Connectors:
(6) Polaris connectors / distribution blocks
Additional Materials:
Conduit and fittings
Wire‑management hardware
Permanent labeling
All materials installed per NEC and local code requirements
---
Labor Requirements
Crew Size: 2 technicians
Estimated Time: 3–4 hours onsite
Work Includes:
Removal of existing wiring (if required)
Installation of all new conductors
Proper termination of all three circuits
Grounding and bonding verification
Final safety checks to ensure NEC‑compliant connections
---
Additional Notes
Two short onsite videos have been recorded and provided to illustrate the existing conditions and the full scope of work required for completion.
All work to be performed in compliance with NEC standards, manufacturer installation requirements, and applicable AHJ guidelines.

1. Repair or Replace Damaged Panel Leads for Non‑Producing Microinverter
The contractor shall:
-Inspect the affected solar module, wiring harness, and microinverter to identify the specific source of failure.
-Verify whether the non-producing microinverter issue is caused by damaged panel leads or other wiring deficiencies.
-Repair damaged leads using manufacturer‑approved connectors, conductors, and weatherproofing materials or replace the leads entirely if -repair is not feasible.
-Test electrical continuity and microinverter functionality after repair or replacement.
-Confirm restored production through system monitoring platform or inverter communication gateway.
-Document all findings and completed repairs for customer records.

Evaluate and Replace Existing Critter Guard
The contractor shall:
-Conduct a full perimeter inspection of the existing critter guard to determine the extent of deterioration, gaps, or installation deficiencies.
-Assess areas of squirrel or wildlife intrusion and identify points where equipment or wiring has been compromised or left vulnerable.
-Remove the ineffective or damaged critter guard from the array perimeter.
-Install a new, durable critter guard system designed for solar arrays, ensuring:
     -Full perimeter coverage
     -Secure attachment that does not penetrate module frames
     -Proper clearance to avoid shading or airflow obstruction
-Verify that all wiring beneath the array is safely repositioned and protected before installing new guards.
-Provide post-installation photos demonstrating full protection.

**Project Title:** Microinverter Replacement and System Enhancement

**Objective:** To replace failed microinverters and enhance system protections and metering capabilities.

**Tasks:**

1. **Return Material Authorization (RMA) Process:**
   - Initiate and complete the RMA process for the replacement of 44 failed microinverters.
   - Coordinate with the supplier for the procurement and shipment of new microinverters.

2. **Installation of Q-Relay:** << Working on if needed 
   - Assess the current system to determine the necessity of installing a Q-relay.
   - If applicable, install a Q-relay to protect the new microinverters against potential Overvoltage Events (OVE) damage.
   - Ensure protection for 4 strings of microinverters as specified.

3. **Communication Cable Installation:**
   - Return to the site equipped with approximately 40 ft of sunlight-resistant 18-4 communications cable.
   - Replace or install the communications cable as needed to ensure reliable communication between system components.

4. **Relocation of Consumption CTs:**
   - Safely relocate the consumption current transformers (CTs) to the line-side feeders of the System Controller.
   - Ensure accurate metering by verifying the correct placement and connection of the CTs.

**Safety Considerations:**
- Adhere to all applicable electrical codes and safety standards during the handling and installation of electrical components.
- Implement lockout/tagout (LOTO) procedures before commencing work on the electrical system to ensure a safe working environment.
- Use personal protective equipment (PPE) such as gloves, safety glasses, and hard hats where necessary.
- Conduct a thorough risk assessment prior to starting the project, identifying any potential hazards associated with confined space or overhead work.

**Expected Approach/Methodology:**
- Prepare a detailed project plan that outlines timelines and delivery expectations for materials.
- Work under the supervision of a qualified electrical technician to ensure compliance with regulatory standards.
- Use systematic troubleshooting protocols to check all connections after installation and ensure functionality of new components.
- Test the entire system post-installation to confirm the operational integrity of the microinverters, Q-relay, communications, and CTs.

**Deliverables:**
- Replacement of 44 microinverters and completion of the RMA process.
- Installed Q-relay with operational verification.
- Installed 18-4 communications cable with testing for functionality.
- Relocated and verified consumption CT placement for accurate metering.

**Completion Timeline:** To be determined after material arrival and scheduling of site visit.

**Scope of Work for Electrical/Solar Maintenance and Service**

**Project Title:** Functional Validation and Maintenance of Solar Power System

**Objective:** To address operational faults detected in the solar power system, specifically the replacement of fuses in the disconnect and troubleshooting of microinverters not reporting.

**Tasks to Be Performed:**

1. **Site Assessment:**
   - Conduct a thorough visual inspection of the entire solar power system including photovoltaic panels, inverters, and electrical disconnects.
   - Review and document live data logs to identify and confirm faults within the system.

2. **Fuse Replacement:**
   - De-energize the disconnect and lockout/tagout (LOTO) the electrical system to ensure safety during maintenance.
   - Remove and replace all faulty fuses within the disconnect as indicated by testing results.
   - Ensure new fuses are compatible with the system specifications and adhere to the manufacturer's recommendations.

3. **Microinverter Troubleshooting:**
   - Inspect all microinverters for signs of physical damage or wear.
   - Verify all connections are secure and all cables are intact, particularly those linked to communication and power.
   - Update firmware if necessary and perform a reset on all affected microinverters to restore functionality.
   - Test each microinverter to confirm they are reporting correctly and integrate with the overall system monitoring platform.

4. **System Testing and Validation:**
   - Re-energize the system following the successful completion of fuse replacement and microinverter repairs.
   - Conduct further live data checks to ensure all components are functioning within normal operational parameters.
   - Document all changes made and confirm that the system returns to optimum performance.

**Safety Considerations:**
- Follow OSHA safety standards and manufacturer guidelines during all maintenance activities.
- Utilize appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) including gloves, helmets, and eye protection.
- Implement lockout/tagout protocols to mitigate any electrical hazards during maintenance.
- Ensure all personnel involved are qualified and aware of potential electrical hazards.

**Expected Approach/Methodology:**
- Utilize a systematic and methodical approach to troubleshoot and resolve the issues detected, including documentation of all findings and repairs conducted.
- Leverage appropriate testing equipment (e.g., multimeters, infrared thermometers) to conduct assessments and validate repairs.
- Maintain open communication with stakeholders regarding the progress and any additional issues encountered during the maintenance process. 

By executing the above tasks comprehensively, the operational integrity of the solar power system will be restored, ensuring optimal performance and reliability.

**Project Title:** Replacement of 30A AC Disconnect with 60A Disconnect and Fuse Replacement

**Overview:**
This scope of work details the tasks necessary for the installation of a new 60A AC disconnect and the removal of incompatible 60A fuses from the existing 30A AC disconnect at the specified site. The goal is to ensure the electrical system operates safely and efficiently within the required parameters.

**Tasks to be Completed:**

1. **Site Assessment:**
   - Conduct a thorough site evaluation to confirm existing wiring configurations, grounding systems, and direct access to the current 30A AC disconnect.
   - Identify all equipment impacted by the disconnect replacement and any potential hazards in the work area.

2. **Preparation:**
   - Notify relevant stakeholders of the planned service outage and secure necessary approvals for the work to proceed.
   - Gather all required materials including a new 60A AC disconnect, appropriate feeder wires, circuit breakers, and safety gear.

3. **Installation of 60A AC Disconnect:**
   - De-energize the current 30A AC disconnect and verify that all circuits are safe to work on via multimeter testing.
   - Remove the existing 30A AC disconnect from its mounting location, ensuring all associated connections are safely disconnected.
   - Install the new 60A AC disconnect in the designated location, ensuring proper alignment and secure mounting.
   - Connect appropriate size feeder wires compliant with electrical codes and ensure compatibility with the new disconnect.

4. **Removal of Current Fuses:**
   - Safely remove the 60A fuses from the existing 30A disconnect, ensuring there is no risk of electrical shock or equipment damage during the process.
   - Dispose of the removed fuses according to local regulations for hazardous waste.

5. **Inspection and Testing:**
   - Once the installation is complete, engage in a comprehensive inspection of all connections to ascertain compliance with applicable safety standards.
   - Energize the new 60A AC disconnect and conduct testing to verify proper operation and load handling.
   - Document all changes made and record any findings during the installation process.

**Safety Considerations:**
- Ensure all personnel involved in the task are equipped with personal protective equipment (PPE), including gloves, safety glasses, and insulated tools.
- Follow lockout/tagout (LOTO) procedures to guarantee that the system remains in a de-energized state during installation.
